title.zh: 卷二十三 列傳第十三 王誕 王華 王惠 王彧
title.en: Volume 23 Biographies 13: Wang Dan, Wang Hua, Wang Hui, Wang Yu
title.raw: 卷二十三 列傳第十三 王誕 王華 王惠 王彧 Volume 23 Biographies 13: Wang Dan, Wang Hua, Wang Hui, Wang Yu

sentences.zh: 列傳第十三

translations.literal: Biographies 13
translations.idiomatic: Biographies 13

sentences.zh: 王誕王華王惠王彧

translations.literal: Wang Dan, Wang Hua, Wang Hui, Wang Yu
translations.idiomatic: Wang Dan, Wang Hua, Wang Hui, and Wang Yu

sentences.zh: 盧循據廣州，以誕為其平南府長史，甚賓禮之。

translations.literal: Lu Xun held Guangzhou and made Dan Chief Clerk of his Pacify-the-South headquarters, treating him with great courtesy as a guest.
translations.idiomatic: When Lu Xun held Guangzhou, he appointed Dan chief clerk of his Pacify-the-South headquarters and honored him as an esteemed guest.

sentences.zh: 誕久客思歸，乃說循曰：「下官與劉鎮軍情味不淺，若得北歸，必蒙任寄。

translations.literal: Dan, long a guest and longing to return home, then persuaded Xun, saying, "Your humble servant and General Liu share no shallow bond of feeling; if I can go north and return, I am sure to receive appointment and trust.
translations.idiomatic: Dan had been away from home for a long time and yearned to return. He persuaded Xun: "General Liu and I are not strangers. If I can go north again, he will surely give me office and trust."

sentences.zh: 」時廣州刺史吳隱之亦為循所拘留，誕又曰：「將軍今留吳公，公私非計。

translations.literal: " At that time the Inspector of Guangzhou, Wu Yinshi, was also detained by Xun, and Dan added, "If the General now keeps Lord Wu, it is no good plan for public or private interest.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Wu Yinshi, inspector of Guangzhou, was also held by Xun. Dan added: "If you keep Lord Wu now, it serves neither the state nor yourself."

sentences.zh: 孫伯符豈不欲留華子魚，但以一境不容二君耳。

translations.literal: Did Sun Bozhang not wish to keep Huizi Yu? It was only that one territory cannot hold two lords.
translations.idiomatic: Did Sun Ce not want to keep Hua Xin? One domain simply cannot accommodate two masters.

sentences.zh: 」於是誕及隱之俱得還。

translations.literal: Thereupon both Dan and Yinshi were able to return.
translations.idiomatic: Dan and Yinshi were both allowed to go home.

sentences.zh: 誕為宋武帝太尉長史，盡心歸奉，帝甚仗之。

translations.literal: Dan served as Chief Clerk to Emperor Wu of Song when he was Grand Commandant, devoting himself utterly in service; the emperor relied on him greatly.
translations.idiomatic: Dan became chief clerk to Liu Yu while he was grand commandant of Song, serving him with complete loyalty, and the emperor came to depend on him heavily.

sentences.zh: 盧循自蔡洲南走，劉毅固求追討。

translations.literal: When Lu Xun fled south from Caizhou, Liu Yi firmly requested pursuit and suppression.
translations.idiomatic: After Lu Xun fled south from Caizhou, Liu Yi pressed hard for a pursuit.

sentences.zh: 誕密白帝曰：「公既平廣固，復滅盧循，則功蓋終古，勳無與二。

translations.literal: Dan secretly reported to the emperor, saying, "Your Grace has already pacified Guanggu and will again destroy Lu Xun; then merit will cover all antiquity and achievement will have no second.
translations.idiomatic: Dan secretly told the emperor: "You have already taken Guanggu and will soon destroy Lu Xun as well. Your achievement will surpass all antiquity and stand without peer."

sentences.zh: 如此大威，豈可使餘人分之？

translations.literal: With such great prestige, how can it be allowed that others share in it?
translations.idiomatic: Can you let anyone else share in glory of that magnitude?

sentences.zh: 毅與公同起布衣，一時相推耳，今既喪敗，不宜復使立功。

translations.literal: Yi rose with Your Grace from common cloth and was promoted together for a time; now that he has suffered defeat, he should not again be allowed to win achievement.
translations.idiomatic: Yi rose with you from common origins and was promoted alongside you for a time. Now that he has been broken, he ought not be given another chance to win glory."

sentences.zh: 」帝納其說。

translations.literal: The emperor accepted his view.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor took his advice.

sentences.zh: 後為吳國內史，母憂去職。

translations.literal: Later he served as Internal Administrator of Wu commandery and left office on mourning for his mother.
translations.idiomatic: He later served as internal administrator of Wu commandery and left office to mourn his mother.

sentences.zh: 武帝伐劉毅，起為輔國將軍，誕固辭，以墨絰從行。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wu attacked Liu Yi, Dan was summoned as General Who Supports the State; Dan firmly declined and followed the campaign wearing unbleached hemp mourning.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wu marched against Liu Yi, Dan was summoned as General Who Supports the State. He firmly declined the post and followed the campaign dressed in mourning hemp.

sentences.zh: 時諸葛長人行太尉留府事，心不自安，武帝甚慮之。

translations.literal: At the time Zhuge Changren was acting for the Grand Commandant in the capital and was ill at ease in his heart; Emperor Wu was very concerned about him.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuge Changren was then left in charge of the grand commandant's office in the capital and felt uneasy; the emperor was deeply worried about him.

sentences.zh: 毅既平，誕求先下。

translations.literal: After Yi was pacified, Dan asked to go down first.
translations.idiomatic: Once Yi had been defeated, Dan asked to go ahead downriver.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「長人似有自疑心，卿詎宜便去？

translations.literal: The emperor said, "Changren seems to harbor self-doubt in his heart; how can you properly leave at once?
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "Changren seems suspicious and unsettled. Can you really leave so soon?"

sentences.zh: 」誕曰：「長人知下官蒙公垂盼，今輕身單下，必當以為無虞，可少安其意。

translations.literal: " Dan said, "Changren knows that your humble servant enjoys Your Grace's favor; if I now go down lightly and alone, he is sure to think there is nothing to fear and his mind can be somewhat eased.
translations.idiomatic: Dan replied, "Changren knows I enjoy your favor. If I go down alone and unencumbered, he will assume there is no danger and calm down a little."

sentences.zh: 」帝笑曰：「卿勇過賁、育矣。

translations.literal: " The emperor laughed and said, "Your courage surpasses Ben and Yu.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor laughed. "Your courage surpasses that of Ben and Yu."

sentences.zh: 」於是先還。

translations.literal: " Thereupon he returned first.
translations.idiomatic: Dan went back first.

sentences.zh: 後卒，追封作唐縣五等侯。

translations.literal: Later he died; posthumously he was enfeoffed as Marquis of Zuotang, fifth rank.
translations.idiomatic: He died later and was posthumously enfeoffed as fifth-rank marquis of Zuotang.

sentences.zh: 子詡早卒。

translations.literal: His son Xu died young.
translations.idiomatic: His son Xu died young.

sentences.zh: 誕兄嘏字偉世，侍中、左戶尚書、始興公。

translations.literal: Dan's elder brother Jia, styled Weishi, was Attendant-in-Ordinary, Director of the Left Households, and Duke of Shixing.
translations.idiomatic: Dan's elder brother Jia, styled Weishi, served as attendant-in-ordinary, director of the left households, and duke of Shixing.

sentences.zh: 嘏子偃。

translations.literal: Jia's son Yan.
translations.idiomatic: Jia's son was Yan.

sentences.zh: 偃字子游，母晉孝武帝女鄱陽公主。

translations.literal: Yan, styled Ziyou, was the son of the Princess of Poyang, daughter of Emperor Xiaowu of Jin.
translations.idiomatic: Yan, styled Ziyou, was born to the Princess of Poyang, a daughter of Emperor Xiaowu of Jin.

sentences.zh: 宋受禪，封永成君。

translations.literal: When Song received the abdication, he was enfeoffed as Lord of Yongcheng.
translations.idiomatic: When Song received the throne, he was enfeoffed as lord of Yongcheng.

sentences.zh: 偃尚宋武帝第二女吳興長公主，諱榮男。

translations.literal: Yan married the second daughter of Emperor Wu of Song, the Princess of Wuxing, taboo name Rongnan.
translations.idiomatic: Yan married Emperor Wu of Song's second daughter, the Princess of Wuxing, whose taboo name was Rongnan.

sentences.zh: 常裸偃縛諸庭樹，時天夜雪，噤凍久之。

translations.literal: She often had Yan stripped naked and bound to the courtyard trees; once when the sky snowed at night, he froze in silence for a long time.
translations.idiomatic: She often had Yan stripped naked and tied to the trees in the courtyard. One snowy night he stood frozen and silent for a long time.

sentences.zh: 偃兄恢排合詬主，乃免。

translations.literal: Yan's elder brother Hui broke down the gate and reviled the mistress, and only then was he released.
translations.idiomatic: Yan's elder brother Hui broke through the gate and berated the princess, and only then was Yan freed.

sentences.zh: 偃謙虛恭謹，不以世事關懷，位右光祿大夫，贈開府儀同三司，諡恭公。

translations.literal: Yan was modest, respectful, and cautious, and did not concern himself with worldly affairs; he reached Grand Master of Splendid Brightness, was posthumously given the same honors as an opening office with tripartite parity, and was given the posthumous title Duke Gong.
translations.idiomatic: Yan was modest, respectful, and cautious and took no interest in worldly affairs. He rose to grand master of splendid brightness and, after death, was granted opening-office honors with tripartite parity and the posthumous title Duke Gong.

sentences.zh: 長子藻，位東陽太守，尚文帝第六女臨川長公主，諱英媛。

translations.literal: His eldest son Zao served as Administrator of Dongyang, married the sixth daughter of Emperor Wen, the Princess of Linchuan, taboo name Yingyuan.
translations.idiomatic: His eldest son Zao served as administrator of Dongyang and married Emperor Wen's sixth daughter, the Princess of Linchuan, taboo name Yingyuan.

sentences.zh: 公主性妒，而藻別愛左右人吳崇祖。

translations.literal: The princess was jealous, while Zao separately loved a man close to him named Wu Chongzu.
translations.idiomatic: The princess was jealous, but Zao kept a separate attachment to a favorite attendant named Wu Chongzu.

sentences.zh: 景和中，主讒之於廢帝，藻下獄死，主與王氏離婚。

translations.literal: In the Jinghe era the princess slandered him to the deposed emperor; Zao was thrown into prison and died, and the princess divorced the Wang family.
translations.idiomatic: During the Jinghe era the princess denounced him to the deposed emperor. Zao was imprisoned and executed, and the princess divorced the Wangs.

sentences.zh: 宋世諸主莫不嚴妒，明帝每疾之。

translations.literal: In the Song age all princesses were fiercely jealous, and Emperor Ming often resented this.
translations.idiomatic: In Song times every princess was fiercely jealous, and Emperor Ming often deplored it.

sentences.zh: 湖熟令袁慆妻以妒賜死，使近臣虞通之撰妒婦記。

translations.literal: The wife of the magistrate of Hushu, Yuan Tao, was sentenced to death for jealousy, and the emperor had a close attendant, Yu Tongzhi, compile a Record of Jealous Wives.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Tao, wife of the magistrate of Hushu, was sentenced to death for jealousy, and the emperor had his close attendant Yu Tongzhi compile a Record of Jealous Wives.

sentences.zh: 左光祿大夫江湛孫學當尚孝武帝女，上乃使人為學作表讓婚曰：

translations.literal: Jiang Xue, grandson of Left Grand Master of Splendid Brightness Jiang Zhan, was about to marry an daughter of Emperor Xiaowu; the emperor therefore had someone write a memorial on Xue's behalf declining the marriage, saying:
translations.idiomatic: Jiang Xue, grandson of Left Grand Master of Splendid Brightness Jiang Zhan, was to marry a daughter of Emperor Xiaowu. The emperor had someone draft a memorial in Xue's name declining the match:

sentences.zh: 伏承詔旨，當以臨汝公主降嬪，榮出望表，恩加典外。

translations.literal: I humbly receive the edict that the Princess of Linyi is to descend in marriage as my consort; glory exceeds what I hoped for, and favor extends beyond ordinary measure.
translations.idiomatic: I humbly receive the edict that the Princess of Linyi is to marry down to me as consort. The honor exceeds anything I could have hoped for, and the grace extends far beyond ordinary measure.

sentences.zh: 顧審輶蔽，伏用憂惶。

translations.literal: Looking back and examining my obscurity, I prostrate myself in worry and fear.
translations.idiomatic: Looking back at my obscurity, I prostrate myself in worry and fear.

sentences.zh: 臣寒門悴族，人凡質陋，閭閻有對，本隔天姻。

translations.literal: Your subject comes from a cold gate and a withered clan, a man of common quality and coarse substance; though there is a match in the lane, by nature it is separated from imperial marriage.
translations.idiomatic: I come from a cold gate and a withered clan, a man of common quality and coarse substance. Though there is a match in the lane, by nature it stands apart from imperial marriage.

sentences.zh: 如臣素流，家貧業寡，年近將冠，皆已有室。

translations.literal: As for one of my humble station, the family is poor and the estate meager; I am nearly at the age of capping, and all already have wives.
translations.idiomatic: For one of my humble station, the family is poor and the estate meager. I am nearly at the age of capping, and all my brothers already have wives.

sentences.zh: 荊釵布裙，足得成禮。

translations.literal: Thorn hairpins and cloth skirts are quite enough to complete marriage.
translations.idiomatic: Thorn hairpins and cloth skirts are quite enough to complete a marriage.

sentences.zh: 每不自解，無偶迄茲，媒訪莫尋，素族弗問。

translations.literal: I never understand myself how, without a match until now, no go-between can be found and no plain clan is asked.
translations.idiomatic: I never understand how, without a match until now, no go-between can be found and no plain clan is asked.

sentences.zh: 自惟門慶，屬降公主，天恩所覃，庸及醜末。

translations.literal: Reflecting on my family's fortune, it now falls to me to receive the princess; heaven's grace reaches even to this ugly last branch.
translations.idiomatic: Reflecting on my family's fortune, it now falls to me to receive the princess. Heaven's grace reaches even to this ugly last branch.

sentences.zh: 懷憂抱惕，慮不獲免，征命所當，果膺茲舉。

translations.literal: Bearing worry and holding fear, I fear I cannot escape; when the summons came, I indeed received this appointment.
translations.idiomatic: Bearing worry and holding fear, I feared I could not escape. When the summons came, I indeed received this appointment.

sentences.zh: 雖門泰宗榮，於臣非幸，仰緣聖貸，冒陳愚實。

translations.literal: Though the gate is grand and the clan honored, for your subject it is no fortune; looking up to heaven's loan, I rashly state my foolish truth.
translations.idiomatic: Though the gate is grand and the clan honored, for me it is no fortune. Looking up to heaven's loan, I rashly state my foolish truth.

sentences.zh: 自晉氏以來，配尚王姬者，雖累經美胄，亟有名才。

translations.literal: Since the Jin house, those matched to royal princesses, though repeatedly from fine pedigrees, often had famous talent.
translations.idiomatic: Since the Jin house, those matched to royal princesses, though repeatedly from fine pedigrees, often possessed famous talent.

sentences.zh: 至如王敦懾氣，桓溫斂威，真長佯愚以求免，子敬灸足以違禍，王偃無仲都之質，而裸雪於北階，何瑀闕龍工之姿，而投軀于深井，謝莊殆自害于蒙叟，殷沖幾不免于強鉏。

translations.literal: As for Wang Dun quelling his spirit, Huan Wen reining in his authority, Zhenchang feigning stupidity to seek escape, Zijing burning his foot to avoid calamity, Wang Yan lacking Zhongdu's quality yet stripped in snow on the northern steps, He Yu lacking the bearing of a dragon artisan yet casting himself into a deep well, Xie Zhuang nearly harming himself like Meng Sou, and Yin Chong almost not escaping the strong hoe.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Dun had to quell his spirit; Huan Wen reined in his authority. Zhenchang feigned stupidity to escape; Zijing burned his foot to avoid calamity. Wang Yan lacked Zhongdu's quality yet was stripped in snow on the northern steps. He Yu lacked the bearing of a dragon artisan yet cast himself into a deep well. Xie Zhuang nearly harmed himself like Meng Sou; Yin Chong almost failed to escape the strong hoe.

sentences.zh: 彼數人者，非無才意，而勢屈於崇貴，事隔于聞覽，吞悲茹氣，無所逃訴。

translations.literal: Those several men were not without talent and intent, yet their power was bent by exalted nobility, affairs were cut off from hearing and seeing, they swallowed grief and endured breath, and had nowhere to flee in appeal.
translations.idiomatic: Those men were not without talent or intent, yet exalted rank bent their power, affairs were cut off from their sight, they swallowed grief and endured humiliation, and had nowhere to appeal.

sentences.zh: 制勒甚於僕隸，防閑過於婢妾，往來出入，人理之常，當待賓客，朋從之義；

translations.literal: Restraint and control were harsher than for servants, guard and confinement exceeded that for maids; coming and going was the constant of human reason, and when guests were to be received it was the meaning of companionship.
translations.idiomatic: Restraint was harsher than for servants; guard and confinement exceeded that for maids. Coming and going is the constant of human life, and receiving guests is the meaning of companionship.

sentences.zh: 而令掃轍息駕，無窺門之期，廢筵抽席，絕接對之理。

translations.literal: Yet they were made to sweep the ruts and halt the carriage, with no day to peek at the gate; feasts were removed and mats withdrawn, and the principle of meeting face to face was cut off.
translations.idiomatic: Yet they were made to sweep the ruts and halt the carriage, with no day to peek at the gate; feasts were removed and mats withdrawn, and the principle of meeting face to face was cut off.

sentences.zh: 非唯交友離異，乃亦兄弟疏闊。

translations.literal: It was not only that friendship was estranged; even brothers grew distant.
translations.idiomatic: Friendship was estranged, and even brothers grew distant.

sentences.zh: 第令受酒肉之賜，制以動靜，監子待錢帛之私，節其言笑。

translations.literal: The younger brother-in-law might receive gifts of wine and meat, and his movements were regulated; the overseer of the son-in-law awaited private gifts of money and silk and regulated his speech and laughter.
translations.idiomatic: The brother-in-law might receive gifts of wine and meat, and his movements were regulated. The overseer of the son-in-law awaited private gifts of money and silk and regulated his speech and laughter.

sentences.zh: 姆奶爭媚，相勸以嚴，尼媼競前，相諂以急。

translations.literal: Wet nurses competed in flattery and urged one another to severity; Buddhist nuns raced forward and flattered one another into urgency.
translations.idiomatic: Wet nurses competed in flattery and urged one another to severity. Buddhist nuns raced forward and flattered one another into urgency.

sentences.zh: 第令必凡庸下才，監子皆葭萌愚豎。

translations.literal: The younger brother-in-law was sure to be a common and mediocre talent, and the overseers of sons-in-law were all ignorant sprouts from humble stock.
translations.idiomatic: The brother-in-law was sure to be a common and mediocre talent, and the overseers of sons-in-law were all ignorant sprouts from humble stock.

sentences.zh: 議舉止則未閑是非，聽言語則謬於虛實。

translations.literal: When conduct was discussed, they did not yet understand right and wrong; when speech was heard, they were mistaken about empty and real.
translations.idiomatic: When conduct was discussed, they did not understand right and wrong. When speech was heard, they were mistaken about what was empty and what was real.

sentences.zh: 姆奶敢恃耆舊，唯贊妒忌，尼媼自唱多知，務檢口舌。

translations.literal: Wet nurses dared rely on age and seniority and only praised jealousy; Buddhist nuns proclaimed themselves full of knowledge and busied themselves checking tongues.
translations.idiomatic: Wet nurses dared rely on age and seniority and only praised jealousy. Buddhist nuns proclaimed themselves full of knowledge and busied themselves checking tongues.

sentences.zh: 其間又有應答問訊，卜筮師母，乃至殘餘飲食，詰辯與誰，衣被故弊，必責頭領。

translations.literal: Among these there were also answers to questions, divining and midwifery, even leftover food and drink, interrogation of with whom, and old and worn clothing that must be traced to whose head and collar.
translations.idiomatic: Among these there were also answers to questions, divining and midwifery, even leftover food and drink interrogated as to with whom, and old worn clothing that must be traced to whose head and collar.

sentences.zh: 又出入之宜，繁省難衷，或進不獲前，或入不聽出。

translations.literal: Again, going out and coming in was hard to harmonize in its complexity; sometimes advancing one could not go forward, or entering one was not allowed to go out.
translations.idiomatic: Going out and coming in was hard to harmonize in its complexity. Sometimes one could not advance when going forward, or could not leave when entering.

sentences.zh: 不入則嫌於欲疏，求出則疑有別意。

translations.literal: Not entering then invited suspicion of wishing estrangement; seeking to go out then aroused doubt of separate intent.
translations.idiomatic: Not entering invited suspicion of wishing estrangement; seeking to go out aroused doubt of separate intent.

sentences.zh: 召必以三晡為期，遣必以日出為限。

translations.literal: Summons had to be by the third quarter of the day as the term, and dismissal had to be by sunrise as the limit.
translations.idiomatic: Summons had to come by the third quarter of the day, and dismissal had to be by sunrise.

sentences.zh: 夕不見晚魄，朝不識曙星。

translations.literal: At evening one did not see the late moon; at dawn one did not know the morning star.
translations.idiomatic: At evening one did not see the late moon; at dawn one did not know the morning star.

sentences.zh: 至於夜步月而弄琴，晝拱袂而披卷，一生之內，與此長乖。

translations.literal: As for walking in moonlight at night and playing the zither, or by day folding sleeves and unrolling scrolls, within one lifetime one was long estranged from these.
translations.idiomatic: Walking in moonlight at night and playing the zither, or by day folding sleeves and unrolling scrolls — within one lifetime one was long estranged from these.

sentences.zh: 又聲影裁聞，則少婢奔迸，裾袂向席，則醜老叢來。

translations.literal: Again, if voice or shadow was barely heard, young maids would rush away; if skirt or sleeve turned toward the mat, ugly old women would swarm in.
translations.idiomatic: If voice or shadow was barely heard, young maids would rush away. If skirt or sleeve turned toward the mat, ugly old women would swarm in.

sentences.zh: 左右整刷，以疑寵見嫌，賓客未冠，以少容致斥。

translations.literal: Attendants grooming themselves were suspected of seeking favor; guests not yet capped were expelled for youthful appearance.
translations.idiomatic: Attendants grooming themselves were suspected of seeking favor. Guests not yet capped were expelled for youthful appearance.

sentences.zh: 禮有列媵，象有貫魚，本無嫚嫡之嫌，豈有輕婦之誚？

translations.literal: Rites had secondary wives in rank, and the image had threaded fish; originally there was no suspicion of slighting the principal wife, so how could there be reproach for slighting a woman?
translations.idiomatic: Rites had secondary wives in rank, and the image had threaded fish. Originally there was no suspicion of slighting the principal wife, so how could there be reproach for slighting a woman?

sentences.zh: 今義絕傍私，虔恭正匹，而每事必言無儀適，設辭輒云輕易我。

translations.literal: Now private attachments are cut off in righteousness and reverent respect is given the proper wife, yet in every matter she says there is no proper ritual, and whenever words are set forth she says I am treated lightly.
translations.idiomatic: Now private attachments are cut off in righteousness and reverent respect is given the proper wife, yet in every matter she says there is no proper ritual, and whenever words are set forth she says I am treated lightly.

sentences.zh: 又竊聞諸主聚集，唯論夫族，緩不足為急者法，急則可為緩者師。

translations.literal: I also secretly hear that when princesses gather they speak only of husbands' clans; what is slow cannot serve as a model for the urgent, but what is urgent can serve as a teacher for the slow.
translations.idiomatic: I also hear that when princesses gather they speak only of husbands' clans. What is slow cannot serve as a model for the urgent, but what is urgent can serve as a teacher for the slow.

sentences.zh: 更相扇誘，本其恒意，不可貸借，固實常辭。

translations.literal: They further incite one another; their constant intent is that lending cannot be allowed, and refusal is indeed the usual phrase.
translations.idiomatic: They further incite one another. Their constant intent is that lending cannot be allowed, and refusal is indeed the usual phrase.

sentences.zh: 或云野敗去，或云人笑我。

translations.literal: Some say the field is ruined and gone, or say people laugh at me.
translations.idiomatic: Some say the field is ruined and gone; others say people laugh at me.

sentences.zh: 雖曰家事，有甚王憲，發口所言，恒同科律。

translations.literal: Though it is called household affair, it is more severe than royal statutes; what is spoken from the mouth is always equal to statutory law.
translations.idiomatic: Though it is called a household affair, it is more severe than royal statutes. What is spoken from the mouth is always equal to statutory law.

sentences.zh: 王藻雖復強佷，頗經學涉，戲笑之事，遂為冤魂。

translations.literal: Wang Zao, though again strong and perverse, had quite passed through learning; matters of jest and laughter thus became a wronged ghost.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Zao, though again strong and perverse, had quite passed through learning. Matters of jest and laughter thus became a wronged ghost.

sentences.zh: 褚曖憂憤，用致夭絕，傷理害義，難以具聞。

translations.literal: Chu Yuan grieved and resented and thereby met early death; injury to principle and harm to righteousness are hard to set forth fully.
translations.idiomatic: Chu Yuan grieved and resented and thereby met early death. Injury to principle and harm to righteousness are hard to set forth fully.

sentences.zh: 夫螽斯之德，實致克昌，專妒之行，有妨繁衍。

translations.literal: The virtue of the katydid in truth brings flourishing increase; exclusive jealousy in conduct has what obstructs propagation.
translations.idiomatic: The virtue of the katydid in truth brings flourishing increase. Exclusive jealousy in conduct obstructs propagation.

sentences.zh: 是以尚主之門，往往絕嗣，駙馬之身，通離釁咎。

translations.literal: Therefore in the gates of those who marry princesses, heirs are often cut off; the bodies of imperial sons-in-law generally meet separation and blame.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore in the gates of those who marry princesses, heirs are often cut off. The bodies of imperial sons-in-law generally meet separation and blame.

sentences.zh: 以臣凡弱，何以克堪。

translations.literal: As your subject is common and weak, how can I bear it?
translations.idiomatic: As I am common and weak, how can I bear it?

sentences.zh: 必將毀族淪門，豈伊身眚？

translations.literal: I am sure to bring ruin to clan and gate; is it only a personal fault?
translations.idiomatic: I am sure to bring ruin to clan and gate. Is it only a personal fault?

sentences.zh: 前後嬰此，其人雖眾，然皆患彰遐邇，事隔天朝，故吞言咽理，無敢論訴。

translations.literal: Before and after, those who suffered this, though many in number, all had their troubles displayed far and near and affairs cut off from the imperial court; therefore they swallowed words and choked on reason, and dared not appeal.
translations.idiomatic: Before and after, those who suffered this, though many in number, all had their troubles displayed far and near and affairs cut off from the imperial court. Therefore they swallowed words and choked on reason, and dared not appeal.

sentences.zh: 臣幸屬聖明，矜照由道，弘物以典，處親以公，臣之鄙懷，可得自盡。

translations.literal: Your subject is fortunate to belong to sage brightness; pity and illumination follow the Way, the broad thing is handled by statute, and kin is treated with fairness; my humble heart can exhaust itself.
translations.idiomatic: I am fortunate to belong to sage brightness. Pity and illumination follow the Way, the broad thing is handled by statute, and kin is treated with fairness. My humble heart can exhaust itself.

sentences.zh: 如臣門分，世荷殊榮，足守前基，便預提拂。

translations.literal: As for my gate's portion, generation after generation it has received extraordinary glory, enough to keep the former base, and already shares in advance support.
translations.idiomatic: As for my gate's portion, generation after generation it has received extraordinary glory, enough to keep the former base, and already shares in advance support.

sentences.zh: 清官顯位，或由才升，一叨婚戚，咸成恩假。

translations.literal: Clear office and illustrious rank may sometimes rise through talent; once touched by marriage kinship, all become grace on loan.
translations.idiomatic: Clear office and illustrious rank may sometimes rise through talent. Once touched by marriage kinship, all become grace on loan.

sentences.zh: 是以仰冒非宜，披露丹實，非唯止陳一己，規全身願，實乃廣申諸門受患之切。

translations.literal: Therefore I rashly take what is not fitting and disclose red truth; it is not only to state myself and plan for the whole body's wish, but truly to broadly declare the keen suffering of the many gates.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore I rashly take what is not fitting and disclose red truth. It is not only to state myself and plan for the whole body's wish, but truly to broadly declare the keen suffering of the many gates.

sentences.zh: 伏願天慈照察，特賜蠲停，使燕雀微群，得保叢蔚，蠢物憐生，自己彌篤。

translations.literal: I humbly wish heaven's compassion to examine and specially grant exemption and halt, so that swallows and sparrows in small flocks can keep the thicket shade, and stupid things pity life and become more devoted to themselves.
translations.idiomatic: I humbly wish heaven's compassion to examine and specially grant exemption and halt, so that swallows and sparrows in small flocks can keep the thicket shade, and stupid things pity life and become more devoted to themselves.

sentences.zh: 若恩詔難降，披請不申，便當刊膚剪發，投山竄海。

translations.literal: If the gracious edict is hard to descend and the open plea is not granted, then I will cut flesh and shear hair and cast myself into mountains and hide in the sea.
translations.idiomatic: If the gracious edict is hard to descend and the open plea is not granted, then I will cut flesh and shear hair and cast myself into mountains and hide in the sea.

sentences.zh: 帝以此表遍示諸主以諷切之，並為戲笑。

translations.literal: The emperor showed this memorial throughout to the princesses to admonish them sharply, and all took it as jest and laughter.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor circulated this memorial among the princesses to admonish them sharply, and all took it as jest and laughter.

sentences.zh: 元徽中，臨川主表求還身王族，守養弱嗣，許之。

translations.literal: In the Yuanhui era the Princess of Linchuan memorialized asking to return to the Wang clan in person and nurture the weak heir; it was granted.
translations.idiomatic: In the Yuanhui era the Princess of Linchuan memorialized asking to return to the Wang clan in person and nurture the weak heir. It was granted.

sentences.zh: 藻弟懋字昌業，光祿大夫，封南鄉侯。

translations.literal: Zao's younger brother Mao, styled Changye, was Grand Master of Splendid Brightness and was enfeoffed as Marquis of Nanxiang.
translations.idiomatic: Zao's younger brother Mao, styled Changye, was grand master of splendid brightness and was enfeoffed as marquis of Nanxiang.

sentences.zh: 懋子瑩。

translations.literal: Mao's son Ying.
translations.idiomatic: Mao's son was Ying.

sentences.zh: 瑩字奉光，選尚宋臨淮公主，拜駙馬都尉。

translations.literal: Ying, styled Fengguang, was selected to marry the Princess of Linhuai of Song and was appointed Commandant of the Imperial Son-in-Law.
translations.idiomatic: Ying, styled Fengguang, was selected to marry the Princess of Linhuai of Song and was appointed commandant of the imperial son-in-law.

sentences.zh: 累遷義興太守，代謝超宗。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly promoted to Administrator of Yixing, succeeding Xie Chaozong.
translations.idiomatic: He was repeatedly promoted to administrator of Yixing, succeeding Xie Chaozong.

sentences.zh: 超宗去郡，與瑩交惡，還都就懋求書屬瑩求一吏，曰：「丈人一旨，如湯澆雪耳。

translations.literal: When Chaozong left the commandery, he and Ying became hostile; returning to the capital he went to Mao and asked for a letter recommending Ying to grant him one clerk, saying, "One word from the elder is like boiling water poured on snow.
translations.idiomatic: When Chaozong left the commandery, he and Ying became hostile. Returning to the capital he went to Mao and asked for a letter recommending that Ying grant him one clerk, saying, "One word from the elder is like boiling water poured on snow."

sentences.zh: 」及至，瑩答旨以公吏不可。

translations.literal: " When he arrived, Ying answered according to principle that a public clerk could not be granted.
translations.idiomatic: When he arrived, Ying answered according to principle that a public clerk could not be granted.

sentences.zh: 超宗往懋處，對諸賓謂懋曰：「湯定不可澆雪。

translations.literal: Chaozong went to Mao's place and, facing the guests, said to Mao, "Boiling water surely cannot melt snow.
translations.idiomatic: Chaozong went to Mao's place and, facing the guests, said to Mao, "Boiling water surely cannot melt snow."

sentences.zh: 」懋面洞赤，唯大恥愧。

translations.literal: " Mao's face turned deep red; he felt only great shame.
translations.idiomatic: Mao's face turned deep red. He felt only great shame.

sentences.zh: 懋後往超宗處，設精白鮑、美鮓、獐肶。

translations.literal: Later Mao went to Chaozong's place, and fine white abalone, fine pickled fish, and venison paunch were set out.
translations.idiomatic: Later Mao went to Chaozong's place, and fine white abalone, fine pickled fish, and venison paunch were set out.

sentences.zh: 懋問那得佳味，超宗詭言義興始見餉；

translations.literal: Mao asked how such fine flavors were obtained; Chaozong falsely said Yixing had just sent them as tribute.
translations.idiomatic: Mao asked how such fine flavors were obtained. Chaozong falsely said Yixing had just sent them as tribute.

sentences.zh: 陽驚曰：「丈人豈應不得邪？

translations.literal: He feigned surprise and said, "How could the elder not have received them?
translations.idiomatic: He feigned surprise and said, "How could the elder not have received them?"

sentences.zh: 」懋大忿，言於朝廷，稱瑩供養不足，坐失郡，廢棄久之。

translations.literal: " Mao was greatly angry and reported to the court that Ying's provisions were insufficient; he lost the commandery for it and was discarded for a long time.
translations.idiomatic: Mao was greatly angry and reported to the court that Ying's provisions were insufficient. He lost the commandery for it and was discarded for a long time.

sentences.zh: 後曆侍中，東陽太守。

translations.literal: Later he successively served as Attendant-in-Ordinary and Administrator of Dongyang.
translations.idiomatic: Later he successively served as attendant-in-ordinary and administrator of Dongyang.

sentences.zh: 以居郡有惠政，遷吳興太守。

translations.literal: Because in governing the commandery he had benevolent administration, he was transferred to Administrator of Wuxing.
translations.idiomatic: Because his governance of the commandery had benevolent administration, he was transferred to administrator of Wuxing.

sentences.zh: 齊明帝勤憂庶政，瑩頻處二郡，皆有能名。

translations.literal: Emperor Ming of Qi diligently attended to the myriad affairs of government; Ying repeatedly held two commanderies and in both had a reputation for competence.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Ming of Qi diligently attended to the myriad affairs of government. Ying repeatedly held two commanderies and in both earned a reputation for competence.

sentences.zh: 還為中領軍隨王長史。

translations.literal: He returned to serve as Chief Clerk to the Prince of Sui, General Who Guards the Army.
translations.idiomatic: He returned to serve as chief clerk to the Prince of Sui, General Who Guards the Army.

sentences.zh: 意不平，改為太子詹事、中領軍。

translations.literal: His mind was not at peace; he was changed to Grand Mentor of the Heir Apparent and General Who Guards the Army.
translations.idiomatic: Dissatisfied, he was reassigned as grand mentor of the heir apparent and general who guards the army.

sentences.zh: 永元初，政由群小，瑩守職而已，不能有所是非。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Yongyuan, government lay in the hands of petty men; Ying kept his post and nothing more, and could not approve or disapprove.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Yongyuan, government lay in the hands of petty men. Ying kept his post and nothing more and could neither approve nor disapprove.

sentences.zh: 及尚書令徐孝嗣誅，瑩頗綜朝政，啟取孝嗣所居宅，及取孝嗣封名枝江縣侯以為己封。

translations.literal: When Director of the Masters of Writing Xu Xiaosi was executed, Ying took comprehensive charge of court governance, memorialized to take Xiaosi's residence, and took Xiaosi's enfeoffment, Marquis of Zhijiang, as his own enfeoffment.
translations.idiomatic: When Director of the Masters of Writing Xu Xiaosi was executed, Ying took comprehensive charge of court governance, memorialized to take Xiaosi's residence, and took Xiaosi's enfeoffment, Marquis of Zhijiang, as his own.

sentences.zh: 從弟亮謂曰：「此非盛德也。

translations.literal: His younger cousin Liang said to him, "This is not abundant virtue."
translations.idiomatic: His younger cousin Liang said to him, "This is not abundant virtue."

sentences.zh: 」瑩怒曰：「我昔從東度為吳興，束身登岸，徐時為宰相，不能見知，相用為領軍長史。

translations.literal: Ying angrily said, "I once crossed east from Wu commandery, body bound and stepping ashore; at that time Xu was chief minister and could not recognize me, yet he used me as chief clerk to the General Who Guards the Army.
translations.idiomatic: Ying angrily said, "I once crossed east from Wu commandery, body bound and stepping ashore. At that time Xu was chief minister and could not recognize me, yet he used me as chief clerk to the General Who Guards the Army.

sentences.zh: 今住其宅，差無多慚。

translations.literal: Now to dwell in his residence is slightly without much shame."
translations.idiomatic: Now to dwell in his residence is only a little shameful."

sentences.zh: 」時人咸謂失德。

translations.literal: People of the time all said he had lost virtue.
translations.idiomatic: People of the time all said he had lost virtue.

sentences.zh: 亮既當朝，於瑩素雖不善，時欲引與同事。

translations.literal: When Liang came into power, though in origin he was not close to Ying, at the time he wished to draw him into shared office.
translations.idiomatic: When Liang came into power, though in origin he was not close to Ying, at the time he wished to draw him into shared office.

sentences.zh: 遷尚書左僕射，未拜；

translations.literal: He was transferred to Left Vice Director of the Masters of Writing, but had not yet received appointment.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to left vice director of the masters of writing but had not yet received appointment.

sentences.zh: 會護軍崔慧景自京口奉江夏王內向，瑩拒慧景於湖頭。

translations.literal: When Protector of the Army Cui Huijing from Jingkou escorted the Prince of Jiangxia inward, Ying repelled Huijing at Hutou.
translations.idiomatic: When Protector of the Army Cui Huijing from Jingkou escorted the Prince of Jiangxia inward, Ying repelled Huijing at Hutou.

sentences.zh: 眾敗，瑩赴水，乘舫入樂遊，因得還台城。

translations.literal: The host was defeated; Ying entered the water, boarded a boat into Leyou, and thereby was able to return to the terrace city.
translations.idiomatic: The host was defeated. Ying entered the water, boarded a boat into Leyou, and thereby was able to return to the terrace city.

sentences.zh: 慧景敗，瑩還居領軍府。

translations.literal: When Huijing was defeated, Ying again resided in the headquarters of the General Who Guards the Army.
translations.idiomatic: When Huijing was defeated, Ying again resided in the headquarters of the General Who Guards the Army.

sentences.zh: 梁武兵至，復假節、都督宮城諸軍事。

translations.literal: When the troops of Emperor Wu of Liang arrived, he was again given provisional credentials and made Commander of All Military Affairs of the Palace City.
translations.idiomatic: When the troops of Emperor Wu of Liang arrived, he was again given provisional credentials and made commander of all military affairs of the palace city.

sentences.zh: 建康平，瑩乃以宅還徐氏。

translations.literal: When Jiankang was pacified, Ying then returned the residence to the Xu clan.
translations.idiomatic: When Jiankang was pacified, Ying then returned the residence to the Xu clan.

sentences.zh: 初為武帝相國左長史，及踐阼，封建城縣公，累遷尚書令。

translations.literal: At first he was Left Chief Clerk to the emperor when he was Prince of the State of Xiang; when he ascended the throne, he was enfeoffed as Duke of Jiancheng and was repeatedly promoted to Director of the Masters of Writing.
translations.idiomatic: At first he was left chief clerk to the emperor when he was Prince of the State of Xiang. When he ascended the throne, he was enfeoffed as duke of Jiancheng and was repeatedly promoted to director of the masters of writing.

sentences.zh: 瑩性清慎，帝深善之。

translations.literal: Ying's nature was pure and cautious; the emperor deeply approved of him.
translations.idiomatic: Ying's nature was pure and cautious, and the emperor deeply approved of him.

sentences.zh: 時有猛獸入郭，上意不悅，以問群臣，群臣莫對。

translations.literal: At the time a fierce beast entered the outer city; the emperor's mind was displeased, and he asked the ministers; none of the ministers answered.
translations.idiomatic: At the time a fierce beast entered the outer city. The emperor's mind was displeased, and he asked the ministers. None answered.

sentences.zh: 瑩在御筵，乃斂板答曰：「昔擊石拊石，百獸率舞。

translations.literal: Ying was at the imperial banquet and, gathering his tablet, answered, "In old times when stones were struck and clapped, a hundred beasts led the dance.
translations.idiomatic: Ying was at the imperial banquet and, gathering his tablet, answered, "In old times when stones were struck and clapped, a hundred beasts led the dance.

sentences.zh: 陛下膺籙御圖，虎象來格。

translations.literal: Your Majesty receives the tally and holds the chart; tigers and elephants come to approach."
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty receives the tally and holds the chart. Tigers and elephants come to approach."

sentences.zh: 」帝大悅，眾咸服焉。

translations.literal: The emperor was greatly pleased, and the host all submitted.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was greatly pleased, and the host all submitted.

sentences.zh: 十五年，位左光祿大夫、開府儀同三司、丹陽尹。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year he reached Left Grand Master of Splendid Brightness, the same honors as an opening office with tripartite parity, and Governor of Danyang.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifteenth year he reached left grand master of splendid brightness, the same honors as an opening office with tripartite parity, and governor of Danyang.

sentences.zh: 既為公，須開黃合。

translations.literal: Having become a duke, he had to open the yellow gate.
translations.idiomatic: Having become a duke, he had to open the yellow gate.

sentences.zh: 宅前促，欲買南鄰朱侃半宅。

translations.literal: The front of the residence was cramped; he wished to buy half the residence of Zhu Kan to the south.
translations.idiomatic: The front of the residence was cramped. He wished to buy half the residence of Zhu Kan to the south.

sentences.zh: 侃懼見侵，貨得錢百萬，瑩乃回合向東。

translations.literal: Kan feared being encroached upon and, bribed, obtained a million cash; Ying then turned the gate to face east.
translations.idiomatic: Kan feared being encroached upon and, bribed, obtained a million cash. Ying then turned the gate to face east.

sentences.zh: 時人為之語曰：「欲向南，錢可貪；

translations.literal: People of the time made a saying of it: "If you wish to face south, money can be coveted;
translations.idiomatic: People of the time made a saying of it: "If you wish to face south, money can be coveted;

sentences.zh: 遂向東，為黃銅。

translations.literal: then facing east is for yellow bronze."
translations.idiomatic: then facing east is for yellow bronze."

sentences.zh: 」及將拜，印工鑄印，六鑄而龜六毀。

translations.literal: When he was about to receive appointment, the seal craftsman cast the seal; six castings and six times the tortoise was destroyed.
translations.idiomatic: When he was about to receive appointment, the seal craftsman cast the seal. Six castings and six times the tortoise was destroyed.

sentences.zh: 及成，頭空不實，補而用之。

translations.literal: When it was finished, the head was hollow and not solid; it was patched and used.
translations.idiomatic: When it was finished, the head was hollow and not solid. It was patched and used.

sentences.zh: 居職六日暴疾薨，諡曰靜恭。

translations.literal: He held office six days and suddenly fell ill and died; his posthumous title was Jinggong.
translations.idiomatic: He held office six days and suddenly fell ill and died. His posthumous title was Jinggong.

sentences.zh: 少子實嗣。

translations.literal: The youngest son Shi succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: The youngest son Shi succeeded.

sentences.zh: 起家秘書郎，尚梁武帝女安吉公主，襲爵建城縣公，為新安太守。

translations.literal: He began his career as a Secretary Gentleman, married the Princess of Anji, daughter of Emperor Wu of Liang, inherited the enfeoffment as Duke of Jiancheng, and served as Administrator of Xin'an.
translations.idiomatic: He began his career as a secretary gentleman, married the Princess of Anji, daughter of Emperor Wu of Liang, inherited the enfeoffment as duke of Jiancheng, and served as administrator of Xin'an.

sentences.zh: 實從兄來郡，就求告。

translations.literal: Shi's elder cousin from the father's line came to the commandery and came to ask for a loan.
translations.idiomatic: Shi's elder cousin from the father's line came to the commandery and came to ask for a loan.

sentences.zh: 實與銅錢五十萬，不聽於郡及道散用。

translations.literal: Shi gave him five hundred thousand cash in copper but did not allow spending in the commandery or on the road.
translations.idiomatic: Shi gave him five hundred thousand cash in copper but did not allow spending in the commandery or on the road.

sentences.zh: 從兄密于郡市貨，還都求利。

translations.literal: The elder cousin secretly traded goods in the commandery market and, returning to the capital, sought profit.
translations.idiomatic: The elder cousin secretly traded goods in the commandery market and, returning to the capital, sought profit.

sentences.zh: 及去郡數十里，實乃知，命追之。

translations.literal: When he had left the commandery several tens of li, Shi then knew and ordered pursuit.
translations.idiomatic: When he had left the commandery several tens of li, Shi then knew and ordered pursuit.

sentences.zh: 呼從兄上岸盤頭，令卒與杖，搏頰乞原，劣得免。

translations.literal: He called the elder cousin ashore, had his head bound in a turban, ordered soldiers to beat him with staves; he beat his cheeks and begged pardon and barely escaped.
translations.idiomatic: He called the elder cousin ashore, had his head bound in a turban, ordered soldiers to beat him with staves. He beat his cheeks and begged pardon and barely escaped.

sentences.zh: 後為南康嗣王湘州長史、長沙郡。

translations.literal: Later he served as Chief Clerk to the Prince of Nankang, heir of Xiang Province, and Administrator of Changsha.
translations.idiomatic: Later he served as chief clerk to the Prince of Nankang, heir of Xiang Province, and administrator of Changsha.

sentences.zh: 王三日出禊，實衣冠傾崎，王性方嚴，見之意殊惡。

translations.literal: On the third day the prince went out for the spring purification; Shi's hat and robes were askew; the prince's nature was square and strict, and on seeing him his mind was especially loathsome.
translations.idiomatic: On the third day the prince went out for the spring purification. Shi's hat and robes were askew. The prince's nature was square and strict, and on seeing him his mind was especially loathsome.

sentences.zh: 實稱主名謂王曰：「蕭玉志念實，殿下何見憎？

translations.literal: Shi called the prince by his given name and said to the prince, "Xiao Yu's thoughts are fixed on Shi; why does Your Highness show dislike?"
translations.idiomatic: Shi called the prince by his given name and said to the prince, "Xiao Yu's thoughts are fixed on Shi. Why does Your Highness show dislike?"

sentences.zh: 」王驚赧即起。

translations.literal: The prince was startled, flushed, and rose at once.
translations.idiomatic: The prince was startled, flushed, and rose at once.

sentences.zh: 後密啟之，因此廢錮。

translations.literal: Later he secretly reported it, and for this reason was imprisoned and confined.
translations.idiomatic: Later he secretly reported it, and for this reason was imprisoned and confined.

sentences.zh: 亮字奉叔，瑩從父弟也。

translations.literal: Liang, styled Fengshu, was Ying's younger cousin from the father's younger brother's line.
translations.idiomatic: Liang, styled Fengshu, was Ying's younger cousin from the father's younger brother's line.

sentences.zh: 父攸字昌達，仕宋位太宰中郎，贈給事黃門侍郎。

translations.literal: His father You, styled Changda, served Song and reached Grand Master in the Grand Mentor's office, and was posthumously given Attendant of the Yellow Gate.
translations.idiomatic: His father You, styled Changda, served Song and reached grand master in the grand mentor's office, and was posthumously given attendant of the yellow gate.

sentences.zh: 亮以名家子，宋末選尚公主，拜駙馬都尉。

translations.literal: As a son of a famous house, at the end of Song he was selected to marry a princess and was appointed Commandant of the Imperial Son-in-Law.
translations.idiomatic: As a son of a famous house, at the end of Song he was selected to marry a princess and was appointed commandant of the imperial son-in-law.

sentences.zh: 歷任秘書丞。

translations.literal: He successively served as Secretary Assistant.
translations.idiomatic: He successively served as secretary assistant.

sentences.zh: 齊竟陵王子良開西邸，延才俊，以為士林館，使工圖其像，亮亦預焉。

translations.literal: When Prince Jingling of Qi, Ziliang, opened the Western Lodge and extended invitation to talented men, making it the Forest of Letters Hall and having artisans paint their images, Liang also participated.
translations.idiomatic: When Prince Jingling of Qi, Ziliang, opened the Western Lodge and extended invitation to talented men, making it the Forest of Letters Hall and having artisans paint their images, Liang also participated.

sentences.zh: 累遷晉陵太守，在職清公，有美政。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly promoted to Administrator of Jinling and, in office, was pure and fair and had fine administration.
translations.idiomatic: He was repeatedly promoted to administrator of Jinling and, in office, was pure and fair and had fine administration.

sentences.zh: 時有晉陵令沈巑之性粗疏，好犯亮諱，亮不堪，遂啟代之。

translations.literal: At the time the magistrate of Jinling, Shen Cuan, was by nature coarse and careless and liked to violate Liang's taboo; Liang could not bear it and therefore memorialized to replace him.
translations.idiomatic: At the time the magistrate of Jinling, Shen Cuan, was by nature coarse and careless and liked to violate Liang's taboo. Liang could not bear it and therefore memorialized to replace him.

sentences.zh: 巑之怏怏，乃造坐云：「下官以犯諱被代，未知明府諱。

translations.literal: Cuan was discontented and therefore came to his seat and said, "Your humble office was replaced for violating taboo; I do not know the lord's taboo.
translations.idiomatic: Cuan was discontented and therefore came to his seat and said, "Your humble office was replaced for violating taboo. I do not know the lord's taboo.

sentences.zh: 若為攸字，當作無骹尊傍犬？

translations.literal: If it is the character You, should it be made as dog beside the honorific without shank?
translations.idiomatic: If it is the character You, should it be made as dog beside the honorific without shank?

sentences.zh: 為犬傍無骹尊？

translations.literal: Or dog beside without shank honorific?
translations.idiomatic: Or dog beside without shank honorific?

sentences.zh: 若是有心攸？

translations.literal: If it is You with heart?
translations.idiomatic: If it is You with heart?

sentences.zh: 無心攸？

translations.literal: You without heart?
translations.idiomatic: You without heart?

sentences.zh: 乞告示。

translations.literal: I beg to be informed."
translations.idiomatic: I beg to be informed."

sentences.zh: 」亮不履下床跣而走，巑之撫掌大笑而去。

translations.literal: Liang did not step down from the bed and ran away barefoot; Cuan clapped his hands, laughed greatly, and left.
translations.idiomatic: Liang did not step down from the bed and ran away barefoot. Cuan clapped his hands, laughed greatly, and left.

sentences.zh: 建武末，累遷吏部尚書。

translations.literal: At the end of Jianwu he was repeatedly promoted to Director of the Masters of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of Jianwu he was repeatedly promoted to director of the masters of personnel.

sentences.zh: 時右僕射江祏管朝政，多所進拔，為士所歸。

translations.literal: At the time Right Vice Director Jiang Si managed court governance and in many cases promoted and advanced men; scholars turned to him.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Right Vice Director Jiang Si managed court governance and in many cases promoted and advanced men. Scholars turned to him.

sentences.zh: 亮自以身居選部，每持異議。

translations.literal: Liang, since he himself held the Selection Department, each time held a different view.
translations.idiomatic: Liang, since he himself held the Selection Department, each time held a different view.

sentences.zh: 始亮未為吏部郎時，以祏帝之內弟，故深友祏。

translations.literal: At first, before Liang was Director of Personnel, because Si was the emperor's younger brother by the mother's side, he therefore befriended Si deeply.
translations.idiomatic: At first, before Liang was director of personnel, because Si was the emperor's younger brother by the mother's side, he therefore befriended Si deeply.

sentences.zh: 祏為之延譽，益為帝所器重。

translations.literal: Si spread reputation for him, and he was all the more valued by the emperor.
translations.idiomatic: Si spread reputation for him, and he was all the more valued by the emperor.

sentences.zh: 至是與祏情好攜薄，祏昵之如初。

translations.literal: At this time his bond with Si was thin and worn, yet Si treated him intimately as at first.
translations.idiomatic: At this time his bond with Si was thin and worn, yet Si treated him intimately as at first.

sentences.zh: 及祏遇誅，群小放命，凡所除拜，悉由內寵，亮弗能止。

translations.literal: When Si met execution, petty men ran wild; all appointments and promotions entirely came from inner favor, and Liang could not stop it.
translations.idiomatic: When Si met execution, petty men ran wild. All appointments and promotions entirely came from inner favor, and Liang could not stop it.

sentences.zh: 外若詳審，內無明鑒，所選用，拘資次而已，當時不謂為能。

translations.literal: Outwardly he seemed careful in examination, inwardly he had no clear mirror; those he selected and used were bound only by qualification and rank, and people of the time did not call him capable.
translations.idiomatic: Outwardly he seemed careful in examination, inwardly he had no clear mirror. Those he selected and used were bound only by qualification and rank, and people of the time did not call him capable.

sentences.zh: 後為尚書左僕射。

translations.literal: Later he served as Left Vice Director of the Masters of Writing.
translations.idiomatic: Later he served as left vice director of the masters of writing.

sentences.zh: 及東昏肆虐，亮取容以免。

translations.literal: When Dong Hun ran wild, Liang took accommodating manner to escape.
translations.idiomatic: When Dong Hun ran wild, Liang took accommodating manner to escape.

sentences.zh: 梁武帝至新林，內外百僚皆道迎，其不能拔者亦間路送誠款，亮獨不遣。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wu of Liang reached Xinlin, inside and outside the hundred officials all went out on the road to welcome; those who could not break free also sent pledges of loyalty by side roads, but Liang alone did not send anyone.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wu of Liang reached Xinlin, inside and outside the hundred officials all went out on the road to welcome. Those who could not break free also sent pledges of loyalty by side roads, but Liang alone did not send anyone.

sentences.zh: 及東昏遇殺，張稷仍集亮等於太極殿前西鍾下坐，議欲立齊湘東嗣王寶晊。

translations.literal: When Dong Hun met killing, Zhang Ji still gathered Liang and others before the western bell under the Hall of Supreme Pole and sat to discuss wishing to establish Prince Bao Zhi of Xiangdong, heir of Qi.
translations.idiomatic: When Dong Hun met killing, Zhang Ji still gathered Liang and others before the western bell under the Hall of Supreme Pole and sat to discuss wishing to establish Prince Bao Zhi of Xiangdong, heir of Qi.

sentences.zh: 領軍瑩曰：「城閉已久，人情離解，征東在近，何不諮問？

translations.literal: Protector of the Army Ying said, "The city has been closed long; popular feeling is scattered and dissolved; the Eastern Expedition is near — why not consult?"
translations.idiomatic: Protector of the Army Ying said, "The city has been closed long. Popular feeling is scattered and dissolved. The Eastern Expedition is near — why not consult?"

sentences.zh: 」張稷又曰：「桀有昏德，鼎遷于殷。

translations.literal: Zhang Ji again said, "Jie had benighted virtue; the tripod moved to Yin.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Ji again said, "Jie had benighted virtue. The tripod moved to Yin.

sentences.zh: 今實微子去殷、項伯歸漢之日。

translations.literal: Today is truly the day of Weizi leaving Yin and Xiang Bo returning to Han."
translations.idiomatic: Today is truly the day of Weizi leaving Yin and Xiang Bo returning to Han."

sentences.zh: 」亮默然。

translations.literal: Liang was silent.
translations.idiomatic: Liang was silent.

sentences.zh: 朝士相次下床，乃遣國子博士范雲齎東昏首送石頭，推亮為首。

translations.literal: Court gentlemen successively stepped down from the bed; then they sent National University Erudite Fan Yun carrying Dong Hun's head to deliver to Shitou, and pushed Liang to be head.
translations.idiomatic: Court gentlemen successively stepped down from the bed. Then they sent National University Erudite Fan Yun carrying Dong Hun's head to deliver to Shitou, and pushed Liang to be head.

sentences.zh: 城平，朝士畢至，亮獨後，裙履見武帝。

translations.literal: When the city was pacified, court gentlemen all arrived; Liang alone came later, skirt and shoes meeting Emperor Wu.
translations.idiomatic: When the city was pacified, court gentlemen all arrived. Liang alone came later, skirt and shoes meeting Emperor Wu.

sentences.zh: 帝謂曰：「顛而不扶，安用彼相？

translations.literal: The emperor said to him, "When one falls and is not supported, of what use is that minister?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said to him, "When one falls and is not supported, of what use is that minister?"

sentences.zh: 」亮曰：「若其可扶，明公豈有今日之舉。

translations.literal: Liang said, "If he could be supported, would the lord not have today's action?"
translations.idiomatic: Liang said, "If he could be supported, would the lord not have today's action?"

sentences.zh: 」因泣而去。

translations.literal: Thereupon he wept and left.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon he wept and left.

sentences.zh: 霸府開，以為大司馬長史。

translations.literal: When the Overlord's headquarters opened, he was made Chief Clerk to the Grand Marshal.
translations.idiomatic: When the Overlord's headquarters opened, he was made chief clerk to the grand marshal.

sentences.zh: 梁台建，授侍中、尚書令，固讓，乃為侍中、中書監，兼尚書令。

translations.literal: When the Liang terrace was established, he was appointed Attendant-in-Ordinary and Director of the Masters of Writing; he firmly declined, and therefore was Attendant-in-Ordinary and Supervisor of the Masters of Writing, concurrently Director of the Masters of Writing.
translations.idiomatic: When the Liang terrace was established, he was appointed attendant-in-ordinary and director of the masters of writing. He firmly declined, and therefore was attendant-in-ordinary and supervisor of the masters of writing, concurrently director of the masters of writing.

sentences.zh: 及受禪，遷侍中、尚書令、中軍將軍，封豫寧縣公。

translations.literal: When he received the abdication, he was transferred to Attendant-in-Ordinary, Director of the Masters of Writing, and General of the Central Army, and was enfeoffed as Duke of Yun'ning.
translations.idiomatic: When he received the abdication, he was transferred to attendant-in-ordinary, director of the masters of writing, and general of the central army, and was enfeoffed as duke of Yun'ning.

sentences.zh: 天監二年，轉左光祿大夫。

translations.literal: In the second year of Tianjian he was transferred to Left Grand Master of Splendid Brightness.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Tianjian he was transferred to left grand master of splendid brightness.

sentences.zh: 元日朝會，亮辭疾不登殿，設饌別省，語笑自若。

translations.literal: On New Year's Day at the court assembly, Liang declined illness and did not ascend the hall; he set out food in a separate office and spoke and laughed as usual.
translations.idiomatic: On New Year's Day at the court assembly, Liang declined illness and did not ascend the hall. He set out food in a separate office and spoke and laughed as usual.

sentences.zh: 數日，詔公卿問訊，亮無病色。

translations.literal: Several days later an edict ordered the dukes and ministers to inquire; Liang had no sick appearance.
translations.idiomatic: Several days later an edict ordered the dukes and ministers to inquire. Liang had no sick appearance.

sentences.zh: 御史中丞樂藹奏亮大不敬，論棄市。

translations.literal: Censor-in-Chief Yue Ai memorialized that Liang was greatly disrespectful and should be sentenced to execution in the marketplace.
translations.idiomatic: Censor-in-Chief Yue Ai memorialized that Liang was greatly disrespectful and should be sentenced to execution in the marketplace.

sentences.zh: 詔削爵，廢為庶人。

translations.literal: An edict stripped his rank and reduced him to commoner.
translations.idiomatic: An edict stripped his rank and reduced him to commoner.

sentences.zh: 四年，帝宴華光殿，求讜言。

translations.literal: In the fourth year the emperor banqueted at the Hall of Splendid Light and sought forthright words.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year the emperor banqueted at the Hall of Splendid Light and sought forthright words.

sentences.zh: 尚書左丞范縝起曰：「司徒謝朏本有虛名，陛下擢之如此；

translations.literal: Left Assistant Director of the Masters of Writing Fan Zhen rose and said, "Minister of Works Xie Tiao originally had empty reputation; Your Majesty promoted him thus;
translations.idiomatic: Left Assistant Director of the Masters of Writing Fan Zhen rose and said, "Minister of Works Xie Tiao originally had empty reputation. Your Majesty promoted him thus;

sentences.zh: 前尚書令王亮頗有政體，陛下棄之如彼。

translations.literal: former Director of the Masters of Writing Wang Liang quite had the substance of governance; Your Majesty discarded him like that.
translations.idiomatic: Former Director of the Masters of Writing Wang Liang quite had the substance of governance. Your Majesty discarded him like that.

sentences.zh: 愚臣所不知。

translations.literal: Your foolish subject does not understand."
translations.idiomatic: Your foolish subject does not understand."

sentences.zh: 」帝變色曰：「卿可更餘言。

translations.literal: The emperor changed color and said, "You may speak otherwise."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor changed color and said, "You may speak otherwise."

sentences.zh: 」縝固執不已，帝不悅。

translations.literal: Zhen firmly held and did not stop; the emperor was displeased.
translations.idiomatic: Zhen firmly held and did not stop. The emperor was displeased.

sentences.zh: 御史中丞任昉因奏縝妄陳褒貶，請免縝官。

translations.literal: Censor-in-Chief Ren Fang therefore memorialized that Zhen rashly stated praise and blame and requested dismissal of Zhen's office.
translations.idiomatic: Censor-in-Chief Ren Fang therefore memorialized that Zhen rashly stated praise and blame and requested dismissal of Zhen's office.

sentences.zh: 詔可。

translations.literal: The edict approved.
translations.idiomatic: The edict approved.

sentences.zh: 亮因屏居閉掃，不通賓客。

translations.literal: Liang therefore lived in seclusion behind closed doors and did not receive guests.
translations.idiomatic: Liang therefore lived in seclusion behind closed doors and did not receive guests.

sentences.zh: 遭母憂，居喪盡禮。

translations.literal: He encountered mourning for his mother and, in mourning residence, exhausted ritual.
translations.idiomatic: He encountered mourning for his mother and, in mourning residence, exhausted ritual.

sentences.zh: 後為中書監，加散騎常侍。

translations.literal: Later he served as Supervisor of the Masters of Writing and was additionally given Regular Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: Later he served as supervisor of the masters of writing and was additionally given regular attendant.

sentences.zh: 卒，諡煬子。

translations.literal: He died; his posthumous title was Yangzi.
translations.idiomatic: He died. His posthumous title was Yangzi.

sentences.zh: 王華字子陵，誕從祖弟也。

translations.literal: Wang Hua, styled Ziling, was Dan's younger cousin from the grandfather's younger brother's line.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Hua, styled Ziling, was Dan's younger cousin from the grandfather's younger brother's line.

sentences.zh: 祖薈，衛將軍、會稽內史。

translations.literal: His grandfather Hui was General of the Guard and Internal Administrator of Kuaiji.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Hui was General of the Guard and internal administrator of Kuaiji.

sentences.zh: 父廞，司徒右長史。

translations.literal: His father Yin was Right Chief Clerk of the Minister of Education.
translations.idiomatic: His father Yin was right chief clerk of the minister of education.

sentences.zh: 晉安帝隆安初，王恭起兵討王國寶，時廞丁母憂在家。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Long'an in the Jin era of Emperor An, Wang Gong raised troops to attack Wang Guobao; at the time Yin was in mourning for his mother at home.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Long'an in the Jin era of Emperor An, Wang Gong raised troops to attack Wang Guobao. At the time Yin was in mourning for his mother at home.

sentences.zh: 恭檄令起兵，廞即聚眾應之，以女為貞烈將軍，以女人為官屬。

translations.literal: Gong's proclamation ordered troops raised; Yin immediately gathered the host and responded, making his daughter General of Steadfast Valor and making women his officials.
translations.idiomatic: Gong's proclamation ordered troops raised. Yin immediately gathered the host and responded, making his daughter General of Steadfast Valor and making women his officials.

sentences.zh: 及國寶死，恭檄廞罷兵。

translations.literal: When Guobao died, Gong's proclamation ordered Yin to disband troops.
translations.idiomatic: When Guobao died, Gong's proclamation ordered Yin to disband troops.

sentences.zh: 廞起兵之際，多所誅戮，至是不復得已，因舉兵以討恭為名。

translations.literal: When Yin raised troops, he in many cases executed and killed; at this time he could not but do otherwise and therefore raised troops under the name of attacking Gong.
translations.idiomatic: When Yin raised troops, he in many cases executed and killed. At this time he could not but do otherwise and therefore raised troops under the name of attacking Gong.

sentences.zh: 恭遣劉牢之擊廞，廞敗走，不知所在。

translations.literal: Gong sent Liu Laozhi to attack Yin; Yin was defeated and fled, and his whereabouts were unknown.
translations.idiomatic: Gong sent Liu Laozhi to attack Yin. Yin was defeated and fled, and his whereabouts were unknown.

sentences.zh: 長子泰為恭所殺。

translations.literal: His eldest son Tai was killed by Gong.
translations.idiomatic: His eldest son Tai was killed by Gong.

sentences.zh: 華時年十三在軍中，與廞相失，隨沙門釋曇冰逃，使提衣襆從後，津邏咸疑焉。

translations.literal: Hua was then thirteen in the army; he and Yin lost one another and, following the monk Shi Tanbing, fled, making him carry clothes bundled behind; ferry guards all suspected them.
translations.idiomatic: Hua was then thirteen in the army. He and Yin lost one another and, following the monk Shi Tanbing, fled, making him carry clothes bundled behind. Ferry guards all suspected them.

sentences.zh: 華行遲，曇冰罵曰：「奴子怠懈，行不及我。

translations.literal: Hua walked slowly; Tanbing cursed, saying, "Slave child lazy and slack, walking not keeping up with me."
translations.idiomatic: Hua walked slowly. Tanbing cursed, saying, "Slave child lazy and slack, walking not keeping up with me."

sentences.zh: 」以杖捶華數十，眾乃不疑，由此得免。

translations.literal: He beat Hua several tens of times with a staff; the host then did not suspect, and thereby they escaped.
translations.idiomatic: He beat Hua several tens of times with a staff. The host then did not suspect, and thereby they escaped.

sentences.zh: 遇赦還吳，以父存沒不測，布衣蔬食，不交遊者十餘年。

translations.literal: Meeting amnesty he returned to Wu; because his father's survival or death was unknown, he wore plain cloth and ate vegetables and did not associate with travelers for more than ten years.
translations.idiomatic: Meeting amnesty he returned to Wu. Because his father's survival or death was unknown, he wore plain cloth and ate vegetables and did not associate with travelers for more than ten years.

sentences.zh: 宋武帝欲收其才用，乃發廞喪，使華制服。

translations.literal: Emperor Wu of Song wished to gather his talent for use and therefore sent out Yin's coffin and had Hua put on mourning dress.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu of Song wished to gather his talent for use and therefore sent out Yin's coffin and had Hua put on mourning dress.

sentences.zh: 服闋，武帝北伐長安，領鎮西將軍、北徐州刺史，辟華為州主簿。

translations.literal: When mourning ended, Emperor Wu on northern expedition to Chang'an held the post of General Who Guards the West and Inspector of North Xuzhou and recruited Hua as Chief Clerk of the province.
translations.idiomatic: When mourning ended, Emperor Wu on northern expedition to Chang'an held the post of General Who Guards the West and Inspector of North Xuzhou and recruited Hua as chief clerk of the province.

sentences.zh: 後為別駕，曆職著稱。

translations.literal: Later he served as Assistant Administrator and, through successive offices, was famed.
translations.idiomatic: Later he served as assistant administrator and, through successive offices, was famed.

sentences.zh: 文帝鎮江陵，為西中郎主簿、諮議參軍。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wen garrisoned Jiangling, Hua served as Chief Clerk of the Western Central Guard and Advisory Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wen garrisoned Jiangling, Hua served as chief clerk of the Western Central Guard and advisory attendant.

sentences.zh: 文帝未親政事，悉委司馬張邵。

translations.literal: Emperor Wen had not yet personally handled government affairs and entirely entrusted them to Marshal Zhang Shao.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen had not yet personally handled government affairs and entirely entrusted them to Marshal Zhang Shao.

sentences.zh: 華性尚物，不欲人在己前。

translations.literal: Hua's nature valued things and did not wish men before himself.
translations.idiomatic: Hua's nature valued precedence and did not wish men before himself.

sentences.zh: 邵性豪，每行來常引夾轂。

translations.literal: Shao's nature was grand; whenever he went out or came in he often drew paired axle-shafts.
translations.idiomatic: Shao's nature was grand. Whenever he went out or came in he often drew paired axle-shafts.

sentences.zh: 華出入乘牽車，從者不過兩三人以矯之。

translations.literal: Hua went out and in riding a single-horse cart; followers did not exceed two or three men to correct this.
translations.idiomatic: Hua went out and in riding a single-horse cart. Followers did not exceed two or three men to correct this.

sentences.zh: 嘗相逢，華陽若不知是邵，謂左右曰：「此鹵簿甚盛，必是殿下。

translations.literal: Once they met; Hua feigned as if not knowing it was Shao and said to attendants, "This guard procession is very grand; it must be His Highness."
translations.idiomatic: Once they met. Hua feigned as if not knowing it was Shao and said to attendants, "This guard procession is very grand. It must be His Highness."

sentences.zh: 」乃下牽車立於道側，及邵至乃驚。

translations.literal: He then descended the single-horse cart and stood at the roadside; when Shao arrived he was startled.
translations.idiomatic: He then descended the single-horse cart and stood at the roadside. When Shao arrived he was startled.

sentences.zh: 邵白服登城，為華所糾，邵坐被征，華代為司馬。

translations.literal: Shao in plain dress ascended the city wall and was impeached by Hua; Shao was demoted and summoned away, and Hua replaced him as marshal.
translations.idiomatic: Shao in plain dress ascended the city wall and was impeached by Hua. Shao was demoted and summoned away, and Hua replaced him as marshal.

sentences.zh: 文帝將入奉大統，以少帝見害，不敢下。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wen was about to enter and uphold the great succession, because the young emperor was harmed, he did not dare descend.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wen was about to enter and uphold the great succession, because the young emperor was harmed, he did not dare descend.

sentences.zh: 華曰：「先帝有大功于天下，四海所服。

translations.literal: Hua said, "The late emperor had great merit for the realm and was served by the four seas.
translations.idiomatic: Hua said, "The late emperor had great merit for the realm and was served by the four seas.

sentences.zh: 雖嗣主不綱，人望未改。

translations.literal: Though the successor lord was without discipline, popular expectation had not changed.
translations.idiomatic: Though the successor lord was without discipline, popular expectation had not changed.

sentences.zh: 徐羨之中才寒士，傅亮布衣諸生，非有晉宣帝、王大將軍之心明矣。

translations.literal: Xu Xianzhi is a man of middling talent and cold scholar; Fu Liang is a common-cloth student — they do not have the hearts of Jin's Emperor Xuan or Grand General Wang; this is clear.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Xianzhi is a man of middling talent and cold scholar. Fu Liang is a common-cloth student. They do not have the hearts of Jin's Emperor Xuan or Grand General Wang. This is clear.

sentences.zh: 畏廬陵嚴斷，將來必不自容。

translations.literal: They fear Luling's severity and decisiveness; in future they are sure not to contain themselves.
translations.idiomatic: They fear Luling's severity and decisiveness. In future they are sure not to contain themselves.

sentences.zh: 殿下寬叡慈仁，天下所知，已且越次奉迎，冀以見德，悠悠之論，殆必不然。

translations.literal: Your Highness is broad, wise, and benevolent; the realm knows it. To go now and receive out of turn, hoping thereby to show virtue — the distant talk will probably not be so.
translations.idiomatic: Your Highness is broad, wise, and benevolent, and the realm knows it. To go now and receive out of turn, hoping thereby to show virtue — the distant talk will probably not be so.

sentences.zh: 羨之、亮、晦又要檀道濟、王弘五人同功，孰肯相讓，勢必不行。

translations.literal: Xianzhi, Liang, and Hui also bound Tan Daoji and Wang Hong, five men of equal merit — who would yield to whom? The situation is sure not to succeed.
translations.idiomatic: Xianzhi, Liang, and Hui also bound Tan Daoji and Wang Hong, five men of equal merit — who would yield to whom? The situation is sure not to succeed.

sentences.zh: 今日就征，萬無所慮。

translations.literal: To go now and accept summons, there is absolutely nothing to worry about.
translations.idiomatic: To go now and accept summons, there is absolutely nothing to worry about.

sentences.zh: 」帝從之，曰：「卿復欲為吾之宋昌矣。

translations.literal: The emperor followed this and said, "You again wish to be my Song Chang."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor followed this and said, "You again wish to be my Song Chang."

sentences.zh: 」乃留華總後任。

translations.literal: He then left Hua in overall charge of rear duties.
translations.idiomatic: He then left Hua in overall charge of rear duties.

sentences.zh: 華以情事異人，未嘗預宴集。

translations.literal: Hua, because affairs and feelings differed from others, never participated in banquet gatherings.
translations.idiomatic: Hua, because affairs and feelings differed from others, never participated in banquet gatherings.

sentences.zh: 終身不飲酒，有宴不之詣。

translations.literal: All his life he did not drink wine; if there was a banquet he did not go.
translations.idiomatic: All his life he did not drink wine. If there was a banquet he did not go.

sentences.zh: 若有論事者，乘車造門，主人出車就之。

translations.literal: If there were matters to discuss, he rode a carriage to the gate; the host came out with a carriage to meet him.
translations.idiomatic: If there were matters to discuss, he rode a carriage to the gate. The host came out with a carriage to meet him.

sentences.zh: 及王弘輔政，而弘弟曇首為文帝所任，與華相埒。

translations.literal: When Wang Hong assisted in governance, Hong's younger brother Tanshou was entrusted by Emperor Wen and was equal to Hua in rank.
translations.idiomatic: When Wang Hong assisted in governance, Hong's younger brother Tanshou was entrusted by Emperor Wen and was equal to Hua in rank.

sentences.zh: 華常謂己力用不盡，每歎曰：「宰相頓有數人，天下何由得安？

translations.literal: Hua often said his strength and use were not exhausted and each time sighed, saying, "The chief minister suddenly has several men; how can the realm be at peace?"
translations.idiomatic: Hua often said his strength and use were not exhausted and each time sighed, saying, "The chief minister suddenly has several men. How can the realm be at peace?"

sentences.zh: 」四年卒，年四十三。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he died, aged forty-three.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year he died, aged forty-three.

sentences.zh: 九年，以誅羨之功，追封新建縣侯，諡曰宣。

translations.literal: In the ninth year, for merit in executing Xianzhi, he was posthumously enfeoffed as Marquis of Xinjian and given the posthumous title Xuan.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year, for merit in executing Xianzhi, he was posthumously enfeoffed as marquis of Xinjian and given the posthumous title Xuan.

sentences.zh: 孝武即位，配享文帝廟庭。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xiaowu ascended the throne, he was granted paired sacrifice in Emperor Wen's temple court.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xiaowu ascended the throne, he was granted paired sacrifice in Emperor Wen's temple court.

sentences.zh: 子定侯嗣，卒。

translations.literal: His son Ding succeeded as marquis and died.
translations.idiomatic: His son Ding succeeded as marquis and died.

sentences.zh: 子長嗣，坐罵母奪爵，以長弟佟詔封。

translations.literal: His son Chang succeeded; for reviling his mother his rank was taken and his younger brother Tong was enfeoffed by edict.
translations.idiomatic: His son Chang succeeded. For reviling his mother his rank was taken and his younger brother Tong was enfeoffed by edict.

sentences.zh: 齊受禪，國除。

translations.literal: When Qi received the abdication, the state was abolished.
translations.idiomatic: When Qi received the abdication, the state was abolished.

sentences.zh: 琨，華從父弟也。

translations.literal: Kun was Hua's younger cousin from the father's younger brother's line.
translations.idiomatic: Kun was Hua's younger cousin from the father's younger brother's line.

sentences.zh: 父懌不辨菽麥，時以為殷道矜之流。

translations.literal: His father Yi could not distinguish beans from wheat and at the time was considered of Yin Daojin's sort.
translations.idiomatic: His father Yi could not distinguish beans from wheat and at the time was considered of Yin Daojin's sort.

sentences.zh: 人無肯與婚，家以獠婢恭心侍之，遂生琨。

translations.literal: No man was willing to marry him; the family had a Liao maidservant named Gongxin who served him devotedly, and thereby Kun was born.
translations.idiomatic: No man was willing to marry him. The family had a Liao maidservant named Gongxin who served him devotedly, and thereby Kun was born.

sentences.zh: 初名昆侖，懌後娶南陽樂玄女，無子，故即以琨為名，立以為嗣。

translations.literal: At first he was named Kunlun; later Yi married the daughter of Le Xuan of Nanyang and had no son, and therefore took Kun as the name and established him as heir.
translations.idiomatic: At first he was named Kunlun. Later Yi married the daughter of Le Xuan of Nanyang and had no son, and therefore took Kun as the name and established him as heir.

sentences.zh: 琨少謹篤，為從伯司徒謐所愛。

translations.literal: Kun in youth was careful and sincere and was loved by his elder cousin from the father's line, Minister of Education Mi.
translations.idiomatic: Kun in youth was careful and sincere and was loved by his elder cousin from the father's line, Minister of Education Mi.

sentences.zh: 宋武帝初為桓修參軍，修待帝厚。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Song Emperor Wu was staff officer to Huan Xiu; Xiu treated the emperor generously.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Song Emperor Wu was staff officer to Huan Xiu. Xiu treated the emperor generously.

sentences.zh: 後帝以事計圖修，猶懷昔顧，使王華訪素門，嫁其二女。

translations.literal: Later the emperor plotted against Xiu because of affairs, yet still cherished former regard and sent Wang Hua to seek a plain gate and marry his two daughters.
translations.idiomatic: Later the emperor plotted against Xiu because of affairs, yet still cherished former regard and sent Wang Hua to seek a plain gate and marry his two daughters.

sentences.zh: 華為琨娶大女，以小女適潁川庾敬度，亦是舊族。

translations.literal: Hua married the elder daughter to Kun and married the younger daughter to Ying Jingdu of Yingchuan, also an old clan.
