translations.idiomatic: Hua married the elder daughter to Kun and married the younger daughter to Ying Jingdu of Yingchuan, also an old clan.

sentences.zh: 除琨郎中、駙馬都尉、奉朝請。

translations.literal: Kun was appointed Palace Gentleman, Commandant of the Imperial Son-in-Law, and Attendant at Court.
translations.idiomatic: Kun was appointed palace gentleman, commandant of the imperial son-in-law, and attendant at court.

sentences.zh: 先是，琨伯父廞得罪晉世，諸子並從誅，唯華得免。

translations.literal: Before this, Kun's father's elder brother Yin had offended in the Jin age; all sons were executed with him, and only Hua escaped.
translations.idiomatic: Before this, Kun's father's elder brother Yin had offended in the Jin age. All sons were executed with him, and only Hua escaped.

sentences.zh: 華宋世貴盛，以門衰，提攜琨，恩若同生，為之延譽。

translations.literal: Hua in the Song age was noble and flourishing; because the gate declined, he raised Kun and treated him with favor as if born together, spreading reputation for him.
translations.idiomatic: Hua in the Song age was noble and flourishing. Because the gate declined, he raised Kun and treated him with favor as if born together, spreading reputation for him.

sentences.zh: 歷位宣城、義熙太守，皆以廉約稱。

translations.literal: He successively served as Administrator of Xuancheng and Yixi and in both was famed for frugality and restraint.
translations.idiomatic: He successively served as administrator of Xuancheng and Yixi and in both was famed for frugality and restraint.

sentences.zh: 華終，又托之宋文帝，故琨屢居清顯。

translations.literal: When Hua died, he again entrusted him to Emperor Wen of Song, and therefore Kun repeatedly held clear and illustrious posts.
translations.idiomatic: When Hua died, he again entrusted him to Emperor Wen of Song, and therefore Kun repeatedly held clear and illustrious posts.

sentences.zh: 孝建中，為吏部郎。

translations.literal: In the Xiaojian era he served as Director of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: In the Xiaojian era he served as director of personnel.

sentences.zh: 吏曹選局，貴要多所屬請，琨自公卿下至士大夫，例為用兩門生。

translations.literal: In the selection bureau of the Personnel Office, the noble and powerful in many cases made requests; Kun from dukes and ministers down to grand masters, as a rule used two student recruits for each.
translations.idiomatic: In the selection bureau of the Personnel Office, the noble and powerful in many cases made requests. Kun from dukes and ministers down to grand masters, as a rule used two student recruits for each.

sentences.zh: 江夏王義恭嘗屬琨用二人，後復屬，琨答不許。

translations.literal: Prince of Jiangxia Yigong once requested Kun to appoint two men; later he again made a request and Kun answered that he would not permit it.
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Jiangxia Yigong once requested Kun to appoint two men. Later he again made a request and Kun answered that he would not permit it.

sentences.zh: 出為平越中郎將、廣州刺史，加都督。

translations.literal: He went out as General of the Center Who Pacifies the Yue and Inspector of Guangzhou, with additional command.
translations.idiomatic: He went out as General of the Center Who Pacifies the Yue and inspector of Guangzhou, with additional command.

sentences.zh: 南土沃實，在任常致巨富。

translations.literal: The southern land was rich and solid; in office he often obtained great wealth.
translations.idiomatic: The southern land was rich and solid. In office he often obtained great wealth.

sentences.zh: 世雲廣州刺史但經城門一過，便得三千萬。

translations.literal: The world said that an Inspector of Guangzhou need only pass the city gate once and would obtain thirty million.
translations.idiomatic: The world said that an inspector of Guangzhou need only pass the city gate once and would obtain thirty million.

sentences.zh: 琨無所取納，表獻祿俸之半。

translations.literal: Kun took nothing in and memorialized presenting half his salary.
translations.idiomatic: Kun took nothing in and memorialized presenting half his salary.

sentences.zh: 鎮舊有鼓吹，又啟輸還。

translations.literal: The garrison originally had martial music; he again memorialized to return it.
translations.idiomatic: The garrison originally had martial music. He again memorialized to return it.

sentences.zh: 及罷任，孝武知其清，問還資多少？

translations.literal: When he left office, Emperor Xiaowu knew his purity and asked how much return capital he had.
translations.idiomatic: When he left office, Emperor Xiaowu knew his purity and asked how much return capital he had.

sentences.zh: 琨曰：「臣買宅百三十萬，餘物稱之。

translations.literal: Kun said, "Your subject bought a residence for one million three hundred thousand; other things match this."
translations.idiomatic: Kun said, "Your subject bought a residence for one million three hundred thousand. Other things match this."

sentences.zh: 」帝悅其對。

translations.literal: The emperor was pleased with his answer.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was pleased with his answer.

sentences.zh: 後為曆陽內史。

translations.literal: Later he served as Internal Administrator of Liyang.
translations.idiomatic: Later he served as internal administrator of Liyang.

sentences.zh: 上以琨忠實，徙為寵子新安王北中郎長史。

translations.literal: The emperor because Kun was loyal and solid transferred him to be Chief Clerk to the Northern Central Guard of the favored son, Prince of Xin'an.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor because Kun was loyal and solid transferred him to be chief clerk to the Northern Central Guard of the favored son, Prince of Xin'an.

sentences.zh: 再曆度支尚書，加光祿大夫。

translations.literal: He again successively served as Director of the Revenue Office and was given Grand Master of Splendid Brightness.
translations.idiomatic: He again successively served as director of the revenue office and was given grand master of splendid brightness.

sentences.zh: 初，琨從兄華孫長襲華爵新建縣侯，嗜酒多愆失，琨表以長將傾基緒，請以長小弟佟嗣焉。

translations.literal: At first Kun's elder cousin Hua's grandson Chang inherited Hua's rank as Marquis of Xinjian; addicted to wine he had many faults; Kun memorialized that Chang would overturn the base and succession and requested that Chang's younger brother Tong succeed.
translations.idiomatic: At first Kun's elder cousin Hua's grandson Chang inherited Hua's rank as Marquis of Xinjian. Addicted to wine he had many faults. Kun memorialized that Chang would overturn the base and succession and requested that Chang's younger brother Tong succeed.

sentences.zh: 琨後出為吳郡太守，遷中領軍，坐在郡用朝舍錢三十六萬，營餉二宮諸王及作絳襖奉獻軍用，左遷光祿大夫。

translations.literal: Later Kun went out as Administrator of Wu commandery and was transferred to General Who Guards the Army; for using thirty-six hundred thousand of the court lodging money in the commandery to supply the two palaces, princes, and make crimson jackets for military use, he was demoted to Grand Master of Splendid Brightness.
translations.idiomatic: Later Kun went out as administrator of Wu commandery and was transferred to General Who Guards the Army. For using thirty-six hundred thousand of the court lodging money in the commandery to supply the two palaces, princes, and make crimson jackets for military use, he was demoted to grand master of splendid brightness.

sentences.zh: 尋加太常及金紫，加散騎常侍。

translations.literal: Soon he was additionally given Grand Master of Ceremonies and gold and purple, and Regular Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was additionally given grand master of ceremonies and gold and purple, and regular attendant.

sentences.zh: 廷尉虞和議社稷各一神，琨案舊糾駁，不為屈。

translations.literal: Court Director of Justice Yu He discussed that the altars of state should each have one spirit; Kun investigated old precedent and impeached, and would not yield.
translations.idiomatic: Court Director of Justice Yu He discussed that the altars of state should each have one spirit. Kun investigated old precedent and impeached, and would not yield.

sentences.zh: 時和見寵，朝廷歎琨強正。

translations.literal: At the time He was favored; the court sighed at Kun's firm uprightness.
translations.idiomatic: At the time He was favored. The court sighed at Kun's firm uprightness.

sentences.zh: 明帝臨崩，出為會稽太守，加都督，坐誤竟囚，降為冠軍。

translations.literal: When Emperor Ming was near death he went out as Administrator of Kuaiji with additional command; for mistakenly releasing a prisoner he was demoted to Champion.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Ming was near death he went out as administrator of Kuaiji with additional command. For mistakenly releasing a prisoner he was demoted to champion.

sentences.zh: 順帝即位，進右光祿大夫。

translations.literal: When Emperor Shun ascended the throne, he was promoted to Right Grand Master of Splendid Brightness.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Shun ascended the throne, he was promoted to right grand master of splendid brightness.

sentences.zh: 順帝遜位，百僚陪列，琨攀畫輪獺尾慟泣曰：「人以壽為歡，老臣以壽為戚。

translations.literal: When Emperor Shun abdicated, the hundred officials accompanied in rank; Kun grasped the painted wheel's otter tail and wept, saying, "Men take longevity as joy; this old minister takes longevity as sorrow.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Shun abdicated, the hundred officials accompanied in rank. Kun grasped the painted wheel's otter tail and wept, saying, "Men take longevity as joy. This old minister takes longevity as sorrow.

sentences.zh: 既不能先驅螻蟻，頻見此事。

translations.literal: I cannot go first as an ant, yet repeatedly see this affair."
translations.idiomatic: I cannot go first as an ant, yet repeatedly see this affair."

sentences.zh: 」嗚噎不自勝，百官人人雨淚。

translations.literal: He sobbed and could not overcome himself; the hundred officials all wept like rain.
translations.idiomatic: He sobbed and could not overcome himself. The hundred officials all wept like rain.

sentences.zh: 琨謙恭謹慎，老而不渝，朝會必早起，簡閱衣裳，料數冠幘，如此數四，或為輕薄所笑。

translations.literal: Kun was modest, respectful, and cautious and in old age did not change; at court assembly he always rose early, examined clothes, counted caps and headcloths — thus several times — and sometimes was laughed at by the frivolous.
translations.idiomatic: Kun was modest, respectful, and cautious and in old age did not change. At court assembly he always rose early, examined clothes, counted caps and headcloths — thus several times — and sometimes was laughed at by the frivolous.

sentences.zh: 大明中，尚書僕射顏師伯豪貴，下省設女樂，琨時為度支尚書，要琨同聽，傳酒行炙，皆悉內妓。

translations.literal: In the Daming era Left Vice Director of the Masters of Writing Yan Shibo was grand and noble; below his office he set out female music; Kun was then Director of the Revenue Office and Shibo invited Kun to listen together; passing wine and serving roast, all were inner courtesans.
translations.idiomatic: In the Daming era Left Vice Director of the Masters of Writing Yan Shibo was grand and noble. Below his office he set out female music. Kun was then director of the revenue office and Shibo invited Kun to listen together. Passing wine and serving roast, all were inner courtesans.

sentences.zh: 琨以男女無親授，傳行每至，令置床上，回面避之然後取，畢又如此，坐上莫不撫手嗤笑，琨容色自若。

translations.literal: Kun because men and women should not touch in passing, each time the pass came he ordered it placed on the bed, turned his face to avoid it and then took it; when finished he again did thus; those seated all clapped hands and laughed, yet Kun's countenance was as usual.
translations.idiomatic: Kun because men and women should not touch in passing, each time the pass came he ordered it placed on the bed, turned his face to avoid it and then took it. When finished he again did thus. Those seated all clapped hands and laughed, yet Kun's countenance was as usual.

sentences.zh: 師伯後為設樂邀琨，琨不往。

translations.literal: Later Shibo again set out music and invited Kun; Kun did not go.
translations.idiomatic: Later Shibo again set out music and invited Kun. Kun did not go.

sentences.zh: 中領軍劉勉，晚節有棲退志，表求東陽郡，尚書令袁粲以下莫不讚美之。

translations.literal: General Who Guards the Army Liu Mian in his late years had intent to withdraw and rest; he memorialized requesting Dongyang commandery; Director of the Masters of Writing Yuan Can and those below all praised it.
translations.idiomatic: General Who Guards the Army Liu Mian in his late years had intent to withdraw and rest. He memorialized requesting Dongyang commandery. Director of the Masters of Writing Yuan Can and those below all praised it.

sentences.zh: 琨曰：「永初、景平，唯謝晦、殷景仁為中領軍，元嘉有到彥之，為人望才譽，勉不及也。

translations.literal: Kun said, "In Yongchu and Jingping, only Xie Hui and Yin Jingren were Generals Who Guard the Army; in Yuanjia there was Dao Yanzhi — in men's expectation and reputation Mian does not reach them.
translations.idiomatic: Kun said, "In Yongchu and Jingping, only Xie Hui and Yin Jingren were generals who guard the army. In Yuanjia there was Dao Yanzhi — in men's expectation and reputation Mian does not reach them.

sentences.zh: 近聞加侍中，已為怏怏，便求東陽，臣恐子房赤松未易輕擬。

translations.literal: Recently I hear he was additionally given Regular Attendant and already was discontent; then he seeks Dongyang — I fear Zifang and Chisong are not easily matched lightly."
translations.idiomatic: Recently I hear he was additionally given regular attendant and already was discontent. Then he seeks Dongyang — I fear Zifang and Chisong are not easily matched lightly."

sentences.zh: 」其鯁直如此。

translations.literal: His blunt uprightness was thus.
translations.idiomatic: His blunt uprightness was thus.

sentences.zh: 而儉於財用，設酒不過兩碗，輒云：「此酒難遇」。

translations.literal: Yet he was frugal in use of wealth; setting out wine did not exceed two bowls, and he would say, "This wine is hard to meet."
translations.idiomatic: Yet he was frugal in use of wealth. Setting out wine did not exceed two bowls, and he would say, "This wine is hard to meet."

sentences.zh: 鹽豉薑蒜之屬，並掛屏風，酒漿悉置床下，內外有求，琨手自賦之。

translations.literal: Salt, fermented beans, ginger, garlic, and the like were all hung on the screen; wine and broth were all placed under the bed; inside and outside if there were requests, Kun personally assigned them.
translations.idiomatic: Salt, fermented beans, ginger, garlic, and the like were all hung on the screen. Wine and broth were all placed under the bed. Inside and outside if there were requests, Kun personally assigned them.

sentences.zh: 景和中，討義陽王昶，六軍戒嚴，應須紫標，左右欲營辦，琨曰：「元嘉初征謝晦，有紫標在匣中，不須更作。

translations.literal: In the Jinghe era when Prince of Yiyang Chang was attacked, the six armies were on alert and purple banners were needed; attendants wished to prepare them; Kun said, "At the beginning of Yuanjia when Xie Hui was attacked, there were purple banners in the box; there is no need to make more."
translations.idiomatic: In the Jinghe era when Prince of Yiyang Chang was attacked, the six armies were on alert and purple banners were needed. Attendants wished to prepare them. Kun said, "At the beginning of Yuanjia when Xie Hui was attacked, there were purple banners in the box. There is no need to make more."

sentences.zh: 」檢取果得焉。

translations.literal: On inspection they were taken out and indeed obtained them.
translations.idiomatic: On inspection they were taken out and indeed obtained them.

sentences.zh: 而避諱過甚，父名懌，母名恭心，並不得犯焉，時咸謂矯枉過正。

translations.literal: Yet he avoided taboo excessively; his father's name was Yi and his mother's name Gongxin — both could not be violated; at the time all said it was correcting excess to excess.
translations.idiomatic: Yet he avoided taboo excessively. His father's name was Yi and his mother's name Gongxin — both could not be violated. At the time all said it was correcting excess to excess.

sentences.zh: 王惠字令明，誕從祖弟也。

translations.literal: Wang Hui, styled Lingming, was Dan's younger cousin from the grandfather's younger brother's line.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Hui, styled Lingming, was Dan's younger cousin from the grandfather's younger brother's line.

sentences.zh: 祖劭，車騎將軍。

translations.literal: His grandfather Shao was General of Chariots and Cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Shao was general of chariots and cavalry.

sentences.zh: 父默，左光祿大夫。

translations.literal: His father Mo was Left Grand Master of Splendid Brightness.
translations.idiomatic: His father Mo was left grand master of splendid brightness.

sentences.zh: 惠幼而夷簡，為叔父司徒謐所知。

translations.literal: Hui in youth was easy and simple and was known by his uncle Minister of Education Mi.
translations.idiomatic: Hui in youth was easy and simple and was known by his uncle Minister of Education Mi.

sentences.zh: 恬靜不交遊，未嘗有雜事。

translations.literal: Tranquil and still, he did not associate in travel and never had miscellaneous affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Tranquil and still, he did not associate in travel and never had miscellaneous affairs.

sentences.zh: 陳郡謝瞻才辯有風氣，嘗與兄弟群從造惠，談論鋒起，文史間發，惠時相詶應，言清理遠，瞻等慚而退。

translations.literal: Xie Zhan of Chen commandery was talented in debate and had spirit; once he and brothers and clan cousins visited Hui; discussion rose sharp and literary and historical matters broke out; Hui at times answered in turn; his words were clear, his reasoning far, and Zhan and the others withdrew in shame.
translations.idiomatic: Xie Zhan of Chen commandery was talented in debate and had spirit. Once he and brothers and clan cousins visited Hui. Discussion rose sharp and literary and historical matters broke out. Hui at times answered in turn. His words were clear, his reasoning far, and Zhan and the others withdrew in shame.

sentences.zh: 宋武帝聞其名，以問其從兄誕，誕曰：「惠後來秀令，鄙宗之美也。

translations.literal: Emperor Wu of Song heard his name and asked his elder cousin Dan; Dan said, "Hui is a later outstanding and fine man, the beauty of our humble clan."
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu of Song heard his name and asked his elder cousin Dan. Dan said, "Hui is a later outstanding and fine man, the beauty of our humble clan."

sentences.zh: 」即以為行參軍，累遷世子中軍長史。

translations.literal: He was therefore made Aide on Campaign and was repeatedly promoted to Chief Clerk of the Heir Apparent's Central Guard.
translations.idiomatic: He was therefore made aide on campaign and was repeatedly promoted to chief clerk of the heir apparent's central guard.

sentences.zh: 時會稽內史劉懷敬之郡，送者傾都，惠亦造別。

translations.literal: At the time Internal Administrator of Kuaiji Liu Huaijing was going to his commandery; those seeing him off filled the capital, and Hui also went to bid farewell.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Internal Administrator of Kuaiji Liu Huaijing was going to his commandery. Those seeing him off filled the capital, and Hui also went to bid farewell.

sentences.zh: 還過從弟球，球問：「向何所見？

translations.literal: Returning he passed his younger cousin Qiu; Qiu asked, "What did you see just now?"
translations.idiomatic: Returning he passed his younger cousin Qiu. Qiu asked, "What did you see just now?"

sentences.zh: 」惠言：「唯覺逢人耳。

translations.literal: Hui said, "I only felt I met people."
translations.idiomatic: Hui said, "I only felt I met people."

sentences.zh: 」素不與謝靈運相識，嘗得交言，靈運辯博，辭義鋒起，惠時然後言。

translations.literal: He had never been acquainted with Xie Lingyun; once he obtained exchange of words; Lingyun was broad in debate and his meaning and words rose sharp; Hui then spoke afterward.
translations.idiomatic: He had never been acquainted with Xie Lingyun. Once he obtained exchange of words. Lingyun was broad in debate and his meaning and words rose sharp. Hui then spoke afterward.

sentences.zh: 時荀伯子在坐，退而告人曰：「靈運固自蕭散直上，王郎有如萬頃陂焉。

translations.literal: At the time Xun Bozi was seated; retiring he told others, "Lingyun is indeed easy and scattered and straight upward; Lord Wang is like a ten-thousand-qing flood plain."
translations.idiomatic: At the time Xun Bozi was seated. Retiring he told others, "Lingyun is indeed easy and scattered and straight upward. Lord Wang is like a ten-thousand-qing flood plain."

sentences.zh: 」嘗臨曲水，風雨暴至，坐者皆馳散。

translations.literal: Once facing the winding stream, wind and rain suddenly arrived; those seated all rushed away.
translations.idiomatic: Once facing the winding stream, wind and rain suddenly arrived. Those seated all rushed away.

sentences.zh: 惠徐起，不異常日，不以沾濡而改。

translations.literal: Hui slowly rose, not different from ordinary days, not changing because of being soaked.
translations.idiomatic: Hui slowly rose, not different from ordinary days, not changing because of being soaked.

sentences.zh: 宋國初建，當置郎中令，武帝難其人，謂傅亮曰：「今用郎中令，不可減袁曜卿。

translations.literal: When the State of Song was first established, a Director of Palace Gentlemen was to be placed; Emperor Wu found the man difficult and said to Fu Liang, "To use a Director of Palace Gentlemen now cannot be less than Lord Yuan Yao."
translations.idiomatic: When the State of Song was first established, a director of palace gentlemen was to be placed. Emperor Wu found the man difficult and said to Fu Liang, "To use a director of palace gentlemen now cannot be less than Lord Yuan Yao."

sentences.zh: 」既而曰：「吾得其人矣，曜卿不得獨擅其奇。

translations.literal: Then he said, "I have obtained the man; Yao cannot alone monopolize the marvel."
translations.idiomatic: Then he said, "I have obtained the man. Yao cannot alone monopolize the marvel."

sentences.zh: 」乃以惠居之。

translations.literal: He therefore placed Hui in it.
translations.idiomatic: He therefore placed Hui in it.

sentences.zh: 兄鑒頗好聚斂，惠意不同，謂曰：「何用田為？

translations.literal: His elder brother Jian quite liked gathering wealth; Hui's mind differed and he said to him, "What use are fields?"
translations.idiomatic: His elder brother Jian quite liked gathering wealth. Hui's mind differed and he said to him, "What use are fields?"

sentences.zh: 」鑒怒曰：「無田何由得食。

translations.literal: Jian angrily said, "Without fields how can one obtain food?"
translations.idiomatic: Jian angrily said, "Without fields how can one obtain food?"

sentences.zh: 」惠又曰：「何用食為？

translations.literal: Hui again said, "What use is food?"
translations.idiomatic: Hui again said, "What use is food?"

sentences.zh: 」其標寄如此。

translations.literal: His lofty intent was thus.
translations.idiomatic: His lofty intent was thus.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈太常，無子。

translations.literal: He died; posthumously he was given Minister of Ceremonies; he had no son.
translations.idiomatic: He died and was posthumously given minister of ceremonies. He had no son.

sentences.zh: 球簡貴勢，不交遊，筵席虛靜，門無異客。

translations.literal: Qiu was simple, noble, and powerful and did not associate in travel; banquets and mats were empty and still and the gate had no strange guests.
translations.idiomatic: Qiu was simple, noble, and powerful and did not associate in travel. Banquets and mats were empty and still and the gate had no strange guests.

sentences.zh: 曇首常云：「蒨玉亦是玉卮無當耳。

translations.literal: Tanshou often said, "Qianyu is also a jade cup without bottom."
translations.idiomatic: Tanshou often said, "Qianyu is also a jade cup without bottom."

sentences.zh: 」既而尚書僕射殷景仁、領軍將軍劉湛並執重權，傾動內外，球雖通家姻戚，未嘗往來。

translations.literal: Then Left Vice Director of the Masters of Writing Yin Jingren and General Who Guards the Army Liu Zhan both held heavy power and moved inside and outside; Qiu though connected by marriage did not ever go back and forth.
translations.idiomatic: Then Left Vice Director of the Masters of Writing Yin Jingren and General Who Guards the Army Liu Zhan both held heavy power and moved inside and outside. Qiu though connected by marriage did not ever go back and forth.

sentences.zh: 居選職，接客甚稀，不視求官書疏，而銓衡有序。

translations.literal: Holding the selection post, he received guests very rarely, did not look at memorials seeking office, yet weighing and balance had order.
translations.idiomatic: Holding the selection post, he received guests very rarely, did not look at memorials seeking office, yet weighing and balance had order.

sentences.zh: 遷光祿大夫，領廬陵王師。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Grand Master of Splendid Brightness and Tutor to the Prince of Luling.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to grand master of splendid brightness and tutor to the Prince of Luling.

sentences.zh: 時大將軍彭城王義康專以政事為本，刀筆幹練者多被意遇。

translations.literal: At the time Grand General Prince of Pengcheng Yikang exclusively took government affairs as the root; men skilled with brush and document and capable were in many cases favored in intent.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Grand General Prince of Pengcheng Yikang exclusively took government affairs as the root. Men skilled with brush and document and capable were in many cases favored in intent.

sentences.zh: 謂劉湛曰：「王敬弘、王球之屬，竟何所堪施？

translations.literal: He said to Liu Zhan, "Men of Wang Jinghong and Wang Qiu's sort — what can they finally be fit to apply?
translations.idiomatic: He said to Liu Zhan, "Men of Wang Jinghong and Wang Qiu's sort — what can they finally be fit to apply?

sentences.zh: 為自富貴，復那可解。

translations.literal: To be for themselves rich and noble — again how can that be understood?"
translations.idiomatic: To be for themselves rich and noble — again how can that be understood?"

sentences.zh: 」球兄子履深結劉湛，委誠義康與劉斌等。

translations.literal: Qiu's elder brother's son Lu deeply attached to Liu Zhan and entrusted sincerity to Yikang and Liu Bin and others.
translations.idiomatic: Qiu's elder brother's son Lu deeply attached to Liu Zhan and entrusted sincerity to Yikang and Liu Bin and others.

sentences.zh: 球每訓厲，不納。

translations.literal: Qiu each time admonished and urged and would not accept.
translations.idiomatic: Qiu each time admonished and urged and would not accept.

sentences.zh: 自大將軍從事中郎轉太子中庶子，流涕訴義康不願違離，故復為從事中郎。

translations.literal: From Attendant in the Grand General's office he was transferred to Junior Mentor of the Heir Apparent; weeping he appealed to Yikang that he did not wish to violate separation and therefore again became attendant in the office.
translations.idiomatic: From attendant in the grand general's office he was transferred to junior mentor of the heir apparent. Weeping he appealed to Yikang that he did not wish to violate separation and therefore again became attendant in the office.

sentences.zh: 文帝甚銜之。

translations.literal: Emperor Wen greatly harbored resentment.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen greatly harbored resentment.

sentences.zh: 及誅湛之夕，履徒跣告球。

translations.literal: On the night Zhan was executed, Lu went barefoot to tell Qiu.
translations.idiomatic: On the night Zhan was executed, Lu went barefoot to tell Qiu.

sentences.zh: 球命為取履，先溫酒與之，謂曰：「常日謂汝何？

translations.literal: Qiu ordered shoes taken for him, first warmed wine and gave it to him, and said, "On ordinary days what did I say to you?"
translations.idiomatic: Qiu ordered shoes taken for him, first warmed wine and gave it to him, and said, "On ordinary days what did I say to you?"

sentences.zh: 」履怖不得答。

translations.literal: Lu was afraid and could not answer.
translations.idiomatic: Lu was afraid and could not answer.

sentences.zh: 球徐曰：「阿父在，汝何憂。

translations.literal: Qiu slowly said, "Father is here; what do you fear?"
translations.idiomatic: Qiu slowly said, "Father is here. What do you fear?"

sentences.zh: 」命左右扶郎還齋，上亦以球故，履免死廢於家。

translations.literal: He ordered attendants to support the young master back to the study; the emperor also because of Qiu's reason spared Lu death and confined him at home.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered attendants to support the young master back to the study. The emperor also because of Qiu's reason spared Lu death and confined him at home.

sentences.zh: 殷景仁卒，球除尚書僕射，王師如故。

translations.literal: When Yin Jingren died, Qiu was appointed Left Vice Director of the Masters of Writing, Tutor unchanged.
translations.idiomatic: When Yin Jingren died, Qiu was appointed left vice director of the masters of writing, tutor unchanged.

sentences.zh: 素有腳疾，多病還家，朝直至少。

translations.literal: He long had foot illness, was often ill and returned home, and attended court rarely.
translations.idiomatic: He long had foot illness, was often ill and returned home, and attended court rarely.

sentences.zh: 錄尚書江夏王義恭謂尚書何尚之曰：「當今乏才，群下宜加戮力，而王球放恣如此，宜以法糾之。

translations.literal: Recorder of the Masters of Writing Prince of Jiangxia Yigong said to Director of the Masters of Writing He Shangzhi, "Today talent is lacking; the host below should add joint strength, yet Wang Qiu is so unrestrained — he should be corrected by law."
translations.idiomatic: Recorder of the Masters of Writing Prince of Jiangxia Yigong said to Director of the Masters of Writing He Shangzhi, "Today talent is lacking. The host below should add joint strength, yet Wang Qiu is so unrestrained — he should be corrected by law."

sentences.zh: 」尚之曰：「球有素尚，加又多疾，公應以淡退求之，未可以文案責也。

translations.literal: Shangzhi said, "Qiu has long had plain intent and moreover has many illnesses; the lord should seek him with mild withdrawal and cannot be charged by documents."
translations.idiomatic: Shangzhi said, "Qiu has long had plain intent and moreover has many illnesses. The lord should seek him with mild withdrawal and cannot be charged by documents."

sentences.zh: 」義恭又面啟文帝曰：「王球誠有素譽，頗以物外自許。

translations.literal: Yigong again face-to-face reported to Emperor Wen, "Wang Qiu indeed has plain reputation and quite takes himself as beyond things.
translations.idiomatic: Yigong again face-to-face reported to Emperor Wen, "Wang Qiu indeed has plain reputation and quite takes himself as beyond things.

sentences.zh: 端任要切，或非所長。

translations.literal: Upright appointment to urgent duty may not be his long suit."
translations.idiomatic: Upright appointment to urgent duty may not be his long suit."

sentences.zh: 」帝曰：「誠知如此，要是時望所歸。

translations.literal: The emperor said, "I truly know it is so, but he is what the times' expectation turns to.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "I truly know it is so, but he is what the times' expectation turns to.

sentences.zh: 昔周伯仁終日飲酒而居此任，蓋所以崇素德也。

translations.literal: In old times Zhou Boren all day drank wine yet held this post — it is to exalt plain virtue."
translations.idiomatic: In old times Zhou Boren all day drank wine yet held this post — it is to exalt plain virtue."

sentences.zh: 」遂見優容。

translations.literal: He was therefore seen with generous tolerance.
translations.idiomatic: He was therefore seen with generous tolerance.

sentences.zh: 後以白衣領職。

translations.literal: Later in plain dress he held the post.
translations.idiomatic: Later in plain dress he held the post.

sentences.zh: 十八年，卒，時年四十九。

translations.literal: In the eighteenth year he died, then aged forty-nine.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighteenth year he died, then aged forty-nine.

sentences.zh: 贈特進、金紫光祿大夫。

translations.literal: Posthumously he was given Special Grand Master and Grand Master of Splendid Brightness with gold and purple.
translations.idiomatic: Posthumously he was given special grand master and grand master of splendid brightness with gold and purple.

sentences.zh: 無子，從孫奐為後。

translations.literal: He had no son; his younger cousin's grandson Huan was made heir.
translations.idiomatic: He had no son. His younger cousin's grandson Huan was made heir.

sentences.zh: 王彧字景文，球從子也。

translations.literal: Wang Yu, styled Jingwen, was Qiu's younger cousin's son.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Yu, styled Jingwen, was Qiu's younger cousin's son.

sentences.zh: 祖穆字伯遠，司徒謐之長兄，位臨海太守。

translations.literal: His grandfather Mu, styled Boyuan, was the eldest elder brother of Minister of Education Mi and reached Administrator of Linhai.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Mu, styled Boyuan, was the eldest elder brother of Minister of Education Mi and reached administrator of Linhai.

sentences.zh: 父僧朗，仕宋位尚書右僕射，明帝初，以後父加特進，贈開府儀同三司，諡元公。

translations.literal: His father Senglang served Song and reached Right Vice Director of the Masters of Writing; at the beginning of Mingdi, as empress's father he was given Special Grand Master, posthumously given the same honors as an opening office with tripartite parity, and posthumous title Duke Yuan.
translations.idiomatic: His father Senglang served Song and reached right vice director of the masters of writing. At the beginning of Mingdi, as empress's father he was given special grand master, posthumously given the same honors as an opening office with tripartite parity, and posthumous title Duke Yuan.

sentences.zh: 彧名與明帝諱同，故以字行。

translations.literal: Yu's name was the same as Emperor Ming's taboo and therefore he was known by his style.
translations.idiomatic: Yu's name was the same as Emperor Ming's taboo and therefore he was known by his style.

sentences.zh: 伯父智少簡貴，有高名，宋武帝甚重之。

translations.literal: His father's elder brother Zhi in youth was simple and noble and had a high name; Emperor Wu of Song greatly valued him.
translations.idiomatic: His father's elder brother Zhi in youth was simple and noble and had a high name. Emperor Wu of Song greatly valued him.

sentences.zh: 常言：「見王智使人思仲祖」。

translations.literal: He often said, "Seeing Wang Zhi makes one think of Zhongzu."
translations.idiomatic: He often said, "Seeing Wang Zhi makes one think of Zhongzu."

sentences.zh: 武帝與劉穆之討劉毅而智在焉，他日，穆之白武帝曰：「伐國重事，公言何乃使王智知。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wu with Liu Muzhi attacked Liu Yi, Zhi was present; another day Muzhi reported to Emperor Wu, "Attacking a state is a weighty affair — why did you let Wang Zhi know?"
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wu with Liu Muzhi attacked Liu Yi, Zhi was present. Another day Muzhi reported to Emperor Wu, "Attacking a state is a weighty affair — why did you let Wang Zhi know?"

sentences.zh: 」武帝笑曰：「此人高簡，豈聞此輩論議。

translations.literal: Emperor Wu laughed and said, "This man is lofty and simple — would he hear this sort of discussion?"
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu laughed and said, "This man is lofty and simple — would he hear this sort of discussion?"

sentences.zh: 」其見知如此。

translations.literal: He was known thus.
translations.idiomatic: He was known thus.

sentences.zh: 為宋國五兵尚書，封建陵縣五等子，追贈太常。

translations.literal: He was Director of the Five Arms of the State of Song, enfeoffed as Viscount of fifth rank of Jianling, and posthumously given Minister of Ceremonies.
translations.idiomatic: He was director of the five arms of the State of Song, enfeoffed as fifth-rank viscount of Jianling, and posthumously given minister of ceremonies.

sentences.zh: 智無子，故父僧朗以景文繼智。

translations.literal: Zhi had no son, and therefore the father Senglang had Jingwen succeed Zhi.
translations.idiomatic: Zhi had no son, and therefore the father Senglang had Jingwen succeed Zhi.

sentences.zh: 幼為從叔球所知憐。

translations.literal: In youth he was known and cherished by his younger uncle Qiu.
translations.idiomatic: In youth he was known and cherished by his younger uncle Qiu.

sentences.zh: 美風姿，為一時推謝。

translations.literal: Fine in bearing and appearance, he was for a time praised by all.
translations.idiomatic: Fine in bearing and appearance, he was for a time praised by all.

sentences.zh: 袁粲見之歎曰：「景文非但風流可悅，乃哺歠亦復可觀。

translations.literal: Yuan Can on seeing him sighed and said, "Jingwen is not only charming and pleasing — even his nursing is also worth viewing."
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Can on seeing him sighed and said, "Jingwen is not only charming and pleasing — even his nursing is also worth viewing."

sentences.zh: 」有一客少時及見謝混，答曰：「景文方謝叔源，則為野父矣。

translations.literal: One guest in youth had seen Xie Hun and answered, "If Jingwen is set beside Uncle Xie, then he is a rustic elder."
translations.idiomatic: One guest in youth had seen Xie Hun and answered, "If Jingwen is set beside Uncle Xie, then he is a rustic elder."

sentences.zh: 」粲惆悵良久，曰：「恨眼中不見此人。」

translations.literal: Can was melancholy a long while and said, "I regret not seeing this man in my eyes."
translations.idiomatic: Can was melancholy a long while and said, "I regret not seeing this man in my eyes."

sentences.zh: 景文好言理，少與陳郡謝莊齊名。

translations.literal: Jingwen liked speaking of principle and in youth was famed equally with Xie Zhuang of Chen commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Jingwen liked speaking of principle and in youth was famed equally with Xie Zhuang of Chen commandery.

sentences.zh: 文帝嘗與群臣臨天泉池，帝垂綸良久不獲。

translations.literal: Emperor Wen once with the host faced the Heavenly Spring Pool; the emperor angled a long while and obtained nothing.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen once with the host faced the Heavenly Spring Pool. The emperor angled a long while and obtained nothing.

sentences.zh: 景文越席曰：「臣以為垂綸者清，故不獲貪餌。

translations.literal: Jingwen crossed the mat and said, "Your subject thinks that he who angles is pure and therefore does not obtain greedy bait."
translations.idiomatic: Jingwen crossed the mat and said, "Your subject thinks that he who angles is pure and therefore does not obtain greedy bait."

sentences.zh: 」眾皆稱善。

translations.literal: The host all praised it as good.
translations.idiomatic: The host all praised it as good.

sentences.zh: 文帝甚相欽重，故為明帝娶景文妹而以景文之名名明帝。

translations.literal: Emperor Wen greatly admired and valued him and therefore had Emperor Ming marry Jingwen's younger sister and named Emperor Ming by Jingwen's given name.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen greatly admired and valued him and therefore had Emperor Ming marry Jingwen's younger sister and named Emperor Ming by Jingwen's given name.

sentences.zh: 武帝第五女新安公主先適太原王景深，離絕，當以適景文，景文固辭以疾，故不成婚。

translations.literal: Emperor Wu's fifth daughter the Princess of Xin'an had first married Wang Jingshen of Taiyuan and separated; she was to marry Jingwen; Jingwen firmly declined on grounds of illness and therefore the marriage was not completed.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu's fifth daughter the Princess of Xin'an had first married Wang Jingshen of Taiyuan and separated. She was to marry Jingwen. Jingwen firmly declined on grounds of illness and therefore the marriage was not completed.

sentences.zh: 襲爵建陵子。

translations.literal: He inherited the rank as Viscount of Jianling.
translations.idiomatic: He inherited the rank as viscount of Jianling.

sentences.zh: 元凶以為黃門侍郎，未及就，孝武入討，景文遣間使歸款。

translations.literal: The crown prince made him Attendant of the Yellow Gate; before he could take up the post, Emperor Xiaowu entered to attack; Jingwen sent a secret messenger to pledge loyalty.
translations.idiomatic: The crown prince made him attendant of the yellow gate. Before he could take up the post, Emperor Xiaowu entered to attack. Jingwen sent a secret messenger to pledge loyalty.

sentences.zh: 以父在都下，不獲致身，事平，頗見嫌責。

translations.literal: Because his father was in the capital he could not devote his person; when affairs were pacified he was quite seen with blame.
translations.idiomatic: Because his father was in the capital he could not devote his person. When affairs were pacified he was quite seen with blame.

sentences.zh: 猶以舊恩，累遷司徒左長史。

translations.literal: Still because of old grace he was repeatedly promoted to Left Chief Clerk of the Minister of Education.
translations.idiomatic: Still because of old grace he was repeatedly promoted to left chief clerk of the minister of education.

sentences.zh: 上以散騎常侍舊與侍中俱掌獻替，欲高其選，以景文及會稽孔覬俱南北之望以補之。

translations.literal: The emperor because Regular Attendant in old times together with Attendant-in-Ordinary jointly held remonstrance and replacement wished to raise the selection and with Jingwen and Kong Xi of Kuaiji, both hopes of north and south, supplemented it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor because regular attendant in old times together with attendant-in-ordinary jointly held remonstrance and replacement wished to raise the selection and with Jingwen and Kong Xi of Kuaiji, both hopes of north and south, supplemented it.

sentences.zh: 尋復為司徒左長史。

translations.literal: Soon he again served as Left Chief Clerk of the Minister of Education.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he again served as left chief clerk of the minister of education.

sentences.zh: 以姊墓開不臨赴，免官。

translations.literal: Because his elder sister's tomb was opened he did not attend in person and was dismissed from office.
translations.idiomatic: Because his elder sister's tomb was opened he did not attend in person and was dismissed from office.

sentences.zh: 後拜侍中、領射聲校尉、左衛將軍，加給事中、太子中庶子。

translations.literal: Later he was appointed Attendant-in-Ordinary, Colonel of the Sound-shooting Guard, and General of the Left Guard, with additional Giver of Affairs and Junior Mentor of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: Later he was appointed attendant-in-ordinary, colonel of the sound-shooting guard, and general of the left guard, with additional giver of affairs and junior mentor of the heir apparent.

sentences.zh: 坐與奉朝請毛法因蒱戲得錢百二十萬，白衣領職。

translations.literal: For with Attendant at Court Mao Fa because of dice play obtaining one million two hundred thousand cash, he held the post in plain dress.
translations.idiomatic: For with attendant at court Mao Fa because of dice play obtaining one million two hundred thousand cash, he held the post in plain dress.

sentences.zh: 景文屢辭內授，上手詔譬之曰：「尚書左僕射，卿已經此任，東宮詹事用人雖美，職次政可比中書令耳。

translations.literal: Jingwen repeatedly declined inner appointment; the emperor by handwritten edict admonished him, saying, "Left Vice Director of the Masters of Writing — you have already held this post; Grand Mentor of the Heir Apparent though the man used is fine, the rank in governance can be compared to Director of the Palace Library.
translations.idiomatic: Jingwen repeatedly declined inner appointment. The emperor by handwritten edict admonished him, saying, "Left vice director of the masters of writing — you have already held this post. Grand mentor of the heir apparent though the man used is fine, the rank in governance can be compared to director of the palace library.

sentences.zh: 庶姓作揚州，徐幹木、王休元、殷鐵並處之不辭，卿清令才望，何愧休元，毗贊中興，豈謝幹木，綢繆相與，何後殷鐵邪？

translations.literal: Common surname as Inspector of Yang Province — Xu Ganmu, Wang Xiuyuan, and Yin Tie all held it and did not decline; you are clear, fine, talented, and hoped for — what shame before Xiuyuan? Assisting the restoration, how is it less than Ganmu? Intimate planning together — how after Yin Tie?"
translations.idiomatic: Common surname as inspector of Yang Province — Xu Ganmu, Wang Xiuyuan, and Yin Tie all held it and did not decline. You are clear, fine, talented, and hoped for — what shame before Xiuyuan? Assisting the restoration, how is it less than Ganmu? Intimate planning together — how after Yin Tie?"

sentences.zh: 司徒以宰相不應帶神州，遠遵先旨，京口鄉基義重，密邇畿內，又不得不用驃騎。

translations.literal: The Minister of Education because the chief minister should not carry the divine province far followed the former intent; Jingkou's native base is weighty in righteousness and close within the capital region — again one cannot but use the General Who Spurs On.
translations.idiomatic: The minister of education because the chief minister should not carry the divine province far followed the former intent. Jingkou's native base is weighty in righteousness and close within the capital region — again one cannot but use the General Who Spurs On.

sentences.zh: 陝西任要，由來用宗室，驃騎既去，巴陵理應居之，中流雖曰閑地，控帶三江，通接荊、郢，經塗之要，由來有重鎮。

translations.literal: Shaanxi's appointment is weighty and from old times used clan members; since the General Who Spurs On has gone, Baling by principle should hold it; the middle stream though called idle land controls the three rivers, connects Jing and Ying, and the route's importance — from old times there has been a heavy garrison.
translations.idiomatic: Shaanxi's appointment is weighty and from old times used clan members. Since the General Who Spurs On has gone, Baling by principle should hold it. The middle stream though called idle land controls the three rivers, connects Jing and Ying, and the route's importance — from old times there has been a heavy garrison.

sentences.zh: 如此，則揚州自成闕刺史。

translations.literal: Thus Yang Province by itself lacks an inspector.
translations.idiomatic: Thus Yang Province by itself lacks an inspector.

sentences.zh: 卿若有辭，便不知誰應處之。

translations.literal: If you have words of decline, then one does not know who should hold it.
translations.idiomatic: If you have words of decline, then one does not know who should hold it.

sentences.zh: 此選大備與公卿疇懷，非聊爾也。

translations.literal: This selection greatly matches the bosom of dukes and ministers — it is not casually done.
translations.idiomatic: This selection greatly matches the bosom of dukes and ministers — it is not casually done.

sentences.zh: 」固辭詹事、領選，徙為中書令，常侍、僕射、揚州如故。

translations.literal: He firmly declined Grand Mentor and holding selection and was transferred to Director of the Palace Library; Regular Attendant, Vice Director, and Yang Province unchanged.
translations.idiomatic: He firmly declined grand mentor and holding selection and was transferred to director of the palace library. Regular attendant, vice director, and Yang Province unchanged.

sentences.zh: 又進中書監，領太子太傅，常侍、揚州如故。

translations.literal: He was further promoted to Supervisor of the Palace Library and Tutor to the Heir Apparent; Regular Attendant and Yang Province unchanged.
translations.idiomatic: He was further promoted to supervisor of the palace library and tutor to the heir apparent. Regular attendant and Yang Province unchanged.

sentences.zh: 景文固辭太傅，上遣新除尚書右僕射褚彥回宣旨，不得已乃受拜。

translations.literal: Jingwen firmly declined Grand Tutor; the emperor sent the newly appointed Right Vice Director of the Masters of Writing Chu Yanhui to announce the intent; unable to do otherwise he then received appointment.
translations.idiomatic: Jingwen firmly declined grand tutor. The emperor sent the newly appointed right vice director of the masters of writing Chu Yanhui to announce the intent. Unable to do otherwise he then received appointment.

sentences.zh: 時太子及諸皇子並小，上稍為身後計，諸將帥吳喜、壽寂之之徒，慮其不能奉幼主，並殺之。

translations.literal: At the time the heir apparent and all princes were still small; the emperor gradually made plans for after his death; the various generals Wu Xi, Shou Jizhi, and the like — fearing they could not serve the young lord — were all killed.
translations.idiomatic: At the time the heir apparent and all princes were still small. The emperor gradually made plans for after his death. The various generals Wu Xi, Shou Jizhi, and the like — fearing they could not serve the young lord — were all killed.

sentences.zh: 而景文外戚貴盛，張永累經軍旅，又疑其將來難信，乃自為謠言曰：「一士不可親，弓長射殺人。

translations.literal: Yet Jingwen as maternal kin was noble and flourishing and Zhang Yong repeatedly passed through campaigns; again he suspected that in future they could not be trusted; he himself made a rhyme saying, "One scholar cannot be intimate; bow long shoots and kills men."
translations.idiomatic: Yet Jingwen as maternal kin was noble and flourishing and Zhang Yong repeatedly passed through campaigns. Again he suspected that in future they could not be trusted. He himself made a rhyme saying, "One scholar cannot be intimate. Bow long shoots and kills men."

sentences.zh: 」一士王字，指景文，弓長張字，指張永。

translations.literal: One scholar is the character Wang and points to Jingwen; bow long is the character Zhang and points to Zhang Yong.
translations.idiomatic: One scholar is the character Wang and points to Jingwen. Bow long is the character Zhang and points to Zhang Yong.

sentences.zh: 景文彌懼，乃自陳求解揚州。

translations.literal: Jingwen was all the more afraid and therefore himself memorialized requesting release from Yang Province.
translations.idiomatic: Jingwen was all the more afraid and therefore himself memorialized requesting release from Yang Province.

sentences.zh: 詔答曰：

translations.literal: The edict answered:
translations.idiomatic: The edict answered:

sentences.zh: 人居貴要，但問心若為耳。

translations.literal: Men dwelling in noble and urgent posts — one need only ask how the heart is.
translations.idiomatic: Men dwelling in noble and urgent posts — one need only ask how the heart is.

sentences.zh: 大明之世，巢、徐二戴位不過執戟，權亢人主；

translations.literal: In the Daming age Chao and Xu, the two Dai, did not exceed halberd-bearing; their power rivaled the lord of men.
translations.idiomatic: In the Daming age Chao and Xu, the two Dai, did not exceed halberd-bearing. Their power rivaled the lord of men.

sentences.zh: 顏師伯白衣僕射，橫行尚書中。

translations.literal: Yan Shibo in plain dress as Vice Director horizontally walked in the Masters of Writing.
translations.idiomatic: Yan Shibo in plain dress as vice director horizontally walked in the masters of writing.

sentences.zh: 袁粲作僕射領選，而人往往不知有粲。

translations.literal: Yuan Can as Vice Director held selection yet men often did not know there was Can.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Can as vice director held selection yet men often did not know there was Can.

sentences.zh: 粲遷為令，居之不疑。

translations.literal: Can was transferred to Director and held it without doubt.
translations.idiomatic: Can was transferred to director and held it without doubt.

sentences.zh: 今既省錄，令便居昔之錄任，置省事及幹僮，並依錄格。

translations.literal: Now since the recorder is reduced, the Director then holds the former recorder's duty; placing clerks and attendants all follows the recorder's standard.
translations.idiomatic: Now since the recorder is reduced, the director then holds the former recorder's duty. Placing clerks and attendants all follows the recorder's standard.

sentences.zh: 粲作令來亦不異為僕射，人情向粲，淡然亦復不改常。

translations.literal: Since Can became Director it is also not different from being Vice Director; men's feeling turns to Can and blandly also does not change the usual.
translations.idiomatic: Since Can became director it is also not different from being vice director. Men's feeling turns to Can and blandly also does not change the usual.

sentences.zh: 以此居貴位要任，當有致憂兢不？

translations.literal: With this dwelling in noble rank and urgent post, should there be causing worry and fear?
translations.idiomatic: With this dwelling in noble rank and urgent post, should there be causing worry and fear?

sentences.zh: 卿今雖作揚州、太子太傅，位雖貴而不關朝政，可安不懼，差於粲也。

translations.literal: You now though holding Yang Province and Grand Tutor to the Heir Apparent — the rank though noble does not touch court governance; can you be secure and not fear? It is less than Can.
translations.idiomatic: You now though holding Yang Province and grand tutor to the heir apparent — the rank though noble does not touch court governance. Can you be secure and not fear? It is less than Can.

sentences.zh: 卿虛心受榮，有而不為累。

translations.literal: You empty-heartedly receive glory and have it yet are not burdened.
translations.idiomatic: You empty-heartedly receive glory and have it yet are not burdened.

sentences.zh: 貴高有危殆之懼，卑賤有溝壑之憂，張單雙災，木雁兩失。

translations.literal: The noble and high have fear of peril; the base and lowly have worry of ditches; single Zhang has double disaster; tree and goose both lose.
translations.idiomatic: The noble and high have fear of peril. The base and lowly have worry of ditches. Single Zhang has double disaster. Tree and goose both lose.

sentences.zh: 有心于避禍，不如無心于任運。

translations.literal: Having heart in avoiding calamity is not as good as having no heart in accepting fate's course.
translations.idiomatic: Having heart in avoiding calamity is not as good as having no heart in accepting fate's course.

sentences.zh: 夫千仞之木，既摧於斧斤，一寸之草，亦悴於踐蹋。

translations.literal: A tree of a thousand ren, once broken by axe and adze; a blade of grass one inch also withers from trampling.
translations.idiomatic: A tree of a thousand ren, once broken by axe and adze. A blade of grass one inch also withers from trampling.

sentences.zh: 高崖之修幹，與深谷之淺條，存亡之要，巨細一揆耳。

translations.literal: High cliff's tall trunk and deep valley's shallow branch — the crux of survival and destruction, great and small, is one measure.
translations.idiomatic: High cliff's tall trunk and deep valley's shallow branch — the crux of survival and destruction, great and small, is one measure.

sentences.zh: 晉將畢萬七戰皆獲，死於牖下，蜀相費禕從容坐談，斃于刺客。

translations.literal: Jin general Bi Wan in seven battles all obtained victory yet died beneath the window; Shu minister Fei Yi calmly sat in talk yet collapsed before assassins.
translations.idiomatic: Jin general Bi Wan in seven battles all obtained victory yet died beneath the window. Shu minister Fei Yi calmly sat in talk yet collapsed before assassins.

sentences.zh: 故甘心于履危，未必逢禍，縱意于處安，不必全福。

translations.literal: Therefore willingly treading danger does not necessarily meet calamity; freely dwelling in safety does not necessarily preserve full blessing.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore willingly treading danger does not necessarily meet calamity. Freely dwelling in safety does not necessarily preserve full blessing.

sentences.zh: 但貴者自惜，故每憂其身，賤者自輕，故易忘其己。

translations.literal: But the noble by themselves cherish themselves and therefore each worry for their person; the base by themselves slight themselves and therefore easily forget themselves.
translations.idiomatic: But the noble by themselves cherish themselves and therefore each worry for their person. The base by themselves slight themselves and therefore easily forget themselves.

sentences.zh: 然為教者每誡貴不誡賤，言其貴滿好自恃也。

translations.literal: Yet those who teach each time admonish the noble and do not admonish the base — they speak of the noble being full and liking to rely on themselves.
translations.idiomatic: Yet those who teach each time admonish the noble and do not admonish the base — they speak of the noble being full and liking to rely on themselves.

sentences.zh: 凡名位貴達，人以存懷，泰則觸人改容，否則行路嗟愕。

translations.literal: Generally name, rank, nobility, and reaching — men because of it store in the bosom; in peace then touching men changes countenance, in decline then passersby sigh in alarm.
translations.idiomatic: Generally name, rank, nobility, and reaching — men because of it store in the bosom. In peace then touching men changes countenance, in decline then passersby sigh in alarm.

sentences.zh: 至如賤者，否泰不足以動人，存亡不足以絓數，死於溝瀆，困于塗路者，天地之間，亦復何限，人不系意耳。

translations.literal: As for the base, decline and peace is insufficient to move men, survival and destruction insufficient to tie numbers; dying in ditches and streams, trapped on the road — between heaven and earth again what limit? Men do not attach mind.
translations.idiomatic: As for the base, decline and peace is insufficient to move men, survival and destruction insufficient to tie numbers. Dying in ditches and streams, trapped on the road — between heaven and earth again what limit? Men do not attach mind.

sentences.zh: 以此而推，貴何必難處，賤何必易安。

translations.literal: Pushing from this, why must the noble be hard to dwell, why must the base be easy to rest?
translations.idiomatic: Pushing from this, why must the noble be hard to dwell, why must the base be easy to rest?

sentences.zh: 但人生自應卑慎為道，行己用心，務思謹惜。

translations.literal: But human life should by itself be base and cautious as the Way; in conduct and use of heart, strive to think carefully and cherish.
translations.idiomatic: But human life should by itself be base and cautious as the Way. In conduct and use of heart, strive to think carefully and cherish.

sentences.zh: 若乃吉凶大期，正應委之理運。

translations.literal: As for the great term of fortune and calamity, one should just entrust it to principle and fate.
translations.idiomatic: As for the great term of fortune and calamity, one should just entrust it to principle and fate.

sentences.zh: 遭隨參差，莫不由命也。

translations.literal: Meeting and following unevenly — none is not from mandate.
translations.idiomatic: Meeting and following unevenly — none is not from mandate.

sentences.zh: 既非聖人，不能見吉凶之先，正是依俙於理，言可行而為之耳。

translations.literal: Since one is not a sage, one cannot see fortune and calamity beforehand — one is just relying on principle, speaking what can be done and doing it.
translations.idiomatic: Since one is not a sage, one cannot see fortune and calamity beforehand — one is just relying on principle, speaking what can be done and doing it.

sentences.zh: 得吉者是其命吉，遇不吉者是其命凶。

translations.literal: Those who obtain fortune — it is their mandate's fortune; those who meet misfortune — it is their mandate's misfortune.
translations.idiomatic: Those who obtain fortune — it is their mandate's fortune. Those who meet misfortune — it is their mandate's misfortune.

sentences.zh: 以近事論之：景和之世，晉平庶人從壽陽歸亂朝，人皆為之戰慄，而乃遇中興之運。

translations.literal: Judging from recent affairs: in the Jinghe age the commoner of Jin Ping returned from Shouyang to the chaotic court; men all for him trembled in fear, yet he then met the restoration's fortune.
translations.idiomatic: Judging from recent affairs: in the Jinghe age the commoner of Jin Ping returned from Shouyang to the chaotic court. Men all for him trembled in fear, yet he then met the restoration's fortune.

sentences.zh: 袁顗圖避禍於襄陽，當時皆羨之，謂為陵霄駕鳳，遂與義嘉同滅。

translations.literal: Yuan Yi plotted to avoid calamity at Xiangyang; at the time all envied him, saying he drove the phoenix to the clouds, yet he together with Yijia perished.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Yi plotted to avoid calamity at Xiangyang. At the time all envied him, saying he drove the phoenix to the clouds, yet he together with Yijia perished.

sentences.zh: 駱宰見狂主，語人言：「越王長頸鳥喙，可與共憂，不可共樂。

translations.literal: Minister Luo saw the mad lord and told men, "The King of Yue had long neck and bird beak — with him one can share worry, not share joy.
translations.idiomatic: Minister Luo saw the mad lord and told men, "The King of Yue had long neck and bird beak — with him one can share worry, not share joy.

sentences.zh: 范蠡去而全身，文種留而遇禍。

translations.literal: Fan Li left and preserved his body; Wen Zhong stayed and met calamity.
translations.idiomatic: Fan Li left and preserved his body. Wen Zhong stayed and met calamity.

sentences.zh: 今主口頸頗有越王之狀，我在尚書中久，不去必危」。

translations.literal: Now the lord's mouth and neck quite has the King of Yue's appearance; I have long been in the Masters of Writing — if I do not go I am sure to be in peril."
translations.idiomatic: Now the lord's mouth and neck quite has the King of Yue's appearance. I have long been in the masters of writing — if I do not go I am sure to be in peril."

sentences.zh: 遂求南江小縣。

translations.literal: He therefore sought a small county on the southern river.
translations.idiomatic: He therefore sought a small county on the southern river.

sentences.zh: 諸都令史住京師者，皆遭中興之慶，人人蒙爵級；

translations.literal: All commandery clerks dwelling in the capital all met the restoration's celebration; each man received rank and grade.
translations.idiomatic: All commandery clerks dwelling in the capital all met the restoration's celebration. Each man received rank and grade.

sentences.zh: 宰逢義嘉染罪，金木纏身，性命幾絕。

translations.literal: The minister met Yijia's tainted crime; metal and wood bound his body and life nearly ended.
translations.idiomatic: The minister met Yijia's tainted crime. Metal and wood bound his body and life nearly ended.

sentences.zh: 卿耳目所聞見，安危在運，何可豫圖邪？

translations.literal: What your ears and eyes have heard and seen — safety and peril lie in fate; how can one plan beforehand?
translations.idiomatic: What your ears and eyes have heard and seen — safety and peril lie in fate. How can one plan beforehand?

sentences.zh: 上既有疾，而諸弟並已見殺；

translations.literal: The emperor already had illness and all younger brothers had already been killed.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor already had illness and all younger brothers had already been killed.

sentences.zh: 唯桂陽王休范人才本劣，不見疑，出為江州刺史。

translations.literal: Only Prince of Guiyang Xiufan by native talent was inferior and was not seen with suspicion; he went out as Inspector of Jiang Province.
translations.idiomatic: Only Prince of Guiyang Xiufan by native talent was inferior and was not seen with suspicion. He went out as inspector of Jiang Province.

sentences.zh: 慮一旦晏駕，皇后臨朝，則景文自然成宰相，門族強盛，藉元舅之重，歲暮不為純臣。

translations.literal: Fearing that once he suddenly died the empress would hold court, then Jingwen naturally would become chief minister; the gate clan was strong and flourishing and relied on the weight of maternal uncle — at year's end he would not be a pure minister.
translations.idiomatic: Fearing that once he suddenly died the empress would hold court, then Jingwen naturally would become chief minister. The gate clan was strong and flourishing and relied on the weight of maternal uncle — at year's end he would not be a pure minister.

sentences.zh: 泰豫元年春，上疾篤，遣使送藥賜景文死，使謂曰：「朕不謂卿有罪，然吾不能獨死，請子先之。

translations.literal: In spring of the first year of Taiyu, the emperor's illness was grave; he sent a messenger delivering medicine granting Jingwen death, and the messenger said, "We did not say you had guilt, yet we cannot die alone — please, sir, go first."
translations.idiomatic: In spring of the first year of Taiyu, the emperor's illness was grave. He sent a messenger delivering medicine granting Jingwen death, and the messenger said, "We did not say you had guilt, yet we cannot die alone — please, sir, go first."

sentences.zh: 」因手詔曰：「與卿周旋，欲全卿門戶，故有此處分。

translations.literal: Thereupon by handwritten edict: "With you circling back and forth, wishing to preserve your gate household — therefore this disposition."
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon by handwritten edict: "With you circling back and forth, wishing to preserve your gate household — therefore this disposition."

sentences.zh: 」敕至之夜，景文政與客棋，扣函看，復還封置局下，神色怡然不變。

translations.literal: When the order arrived that night, Jingwen was just playing weiqi with a guest; he knocked open the case and looked, again sealed it and placed it under the board; his expression was easy and unchanged.
translations.idiomatic: When the order arrived that night, Jingwen was just playing weiqi with a guest. He knocked open the case and looked, again sealed it and placed it under the board. His expression was easy and unchanged.

sentences.zh: 方與客棋思行爭劫竟，斂子內奩畢，徐謂客曰：「奉敕見賜以死。

translations.literal: Just as he and the guest finished thinking through a contested capture, gathered the stones into the box and finished, he slowly said to the guest, "By decree I am granted death."
translations.idiomatic: Just as he and the guest finished thinking through a contested capture, gathered the stones into the box and finished, he slowly said to the guest, "By decree I am granted death."

sentences.zh: 」方以敕示客。

translations.literal: Then he showed the guest the decree.
translations.idiomatic: Then he showed the guest the decree.

sentences.zh: 酒至未飲，門客焦度在側，憤怒發酒覆地曰：「大丈夫安能坐受死。

translations.literal: Wine arrived and he had not yet drunk; the gate guest Jiao Du at the side angrily overturned the wine on the ground and said, "A great man — how can he sit and receive death?
translations.idiomatic: Wine arrived and he had not yet drunk. The gate guest Jiao Du at the side angrily overturned the wine on the ground and said, "A great man — how can he sit and receive death?

sentences.zh: 州中文武可數百人，足以一奮。

translations.literal: Civil and military in the province can be counted in the hundreds — enough for one effort."
translations.idiomatic: Civil and military in the province can be counted in the hundreds — enough for one effort."

sentences.zh: 」景文曰：「知卿至心；

translations.literal: Jingwen said, "I know your utmost heart.
translations.idiomatic: Jingwen said, "I know your utmost heart.

sentences.zh: 若見念者，為我百口計。

translations.literal: If you think of me, plan for my hundred mouths."
translations.idiomatic: If you think of me, plan for my hundred mouths."

sentences.zh: 」乃墨啟答敕，並謝贈詔。

translations.literal: He then in ink opened and answered the decree and also thanked the gift edict.
translations.idiomatic: He then in ink opened and answered the decree and also thanked the gift edict.

sentences.zh: 酌謂客曰：「此酒不可相勸。

translations.literal: He poured and said to the guest, "This wine cannot be mutually urged."
translations.idiomatic: He poured and said to the guest, "This wine cannot be mutually urged."

sentences.zh: 」自仰而飲之。

translations.literal: He himself looked up and drank it.
translations.idiomatic: He himself looked up and drank it.

sentences.zh: 時年六十。

translations.literal: He was then aged sixty.
translations.idiomatic: He was then aged sixty.

sentences.zh: 追贈開府儀同三司，諡曰懿。

translations.literal: Posthumously he was given the same honors as an opening office with tripartite parity and posthumous title Yi.
translations.idiomatic: Posthumously he was given the same honors as an opening office with tripartite parity and posthumous title Yi.

sentences.zh: 長子絢。

translations.literal: His eldest son Xuan.
translations.idiomatic: His eldest son was Xuan.

sentences.zh: 絢字長素，早惠。

translations.literal: Xuan, styled Changsu, was precocious in youth.
translations.idiomatic: Xuan, styled Changsu, was precocious in youth.

sentences.zh: 年五六歲，讀論語至「周監於二代」，外祖何尚之戲之曰：「可改耶耶乎文哉。

translations.literal: Aged five or six, reading the Analects to "Zhou looked to the two dynasties," his maternal grandfather He Shangzhi jested with him, "Can it be changed — yayu wen zai?"
translations.idiomatic: Aged five or six, reading the Analects to "Zhou looked to the two dynasties," his maternal grandfather He Shangzhi jested with him, "Can it be changed — yayu wen zai?"

sentences.zh: 」絢應聲答曰：「尊者之名，安可戲，寧可道草翁之風必舅？

translations.literal: Xuan answered on the sound, "An honored person's name — how can it be jested? Better to say caoweng zhi feng bi jiu?"
translations.idiomatic: Xuan answered on the sound, "An honored person's name — how can it be jested? Better to say caoweng zhi feng bi jiu?"

sentences.zh: 」及長，篤志好學。

translations.literal: When grown, he was devoted in will and loved learning.
translations.idiomatic: When grown, he was devoted in will and loved learning.

sentences.zh: 位秘書丞。

translations.literal: He reached Secretary Assistant.
translations.idiomatic: He reached secretary assistant.

sentences.zh: 先景文卒，諡曰恭世子。

translations.literal: He died before Jingwen and was given posthumous title Gong heir.
translations.idiomatic: He died before Jingwen and was given posthumous title Gong heir.

sentences.zh: 絢弟繢。

translations.literal: Xuan's younger brother Hui.
translations.idiomatic: Xuan's younger brother was Hui.

sentences.zh: 繢字叔素，弱冠秘書郎、太子舍人，轉中書舍人。

translations.literal: Hui, styled Shusu, at weak cap served as Secretary Gentleman and Attendant of the Heir Apparent and was transferred to Palace Library Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: Hui, styled Shusu, at weak cap served as secretary gentleman and attendant of the heir apparent and was transferred to palace library attendant.

sentences.zh: 景文以此授超階，令繢經年乃受。

translations.literal: Jingwen because this appointment exceeded rank ordered Hui to receive it only after a full year.
translations.idiomatic: Jingwen because this appointment exceeded rank ordered Hui to receive it only after a full year.

sentences.zh: 景文封江安侯，繢襲其本爵為始平縣五等男。

translations.literal: Jingwen was enfeoffed as Marquis of Jiang'an; Hui inherited his original rank as Viscount of fifth rank of Shiping.
translations.idiomatic: Jingwen was enfeoffed as marquis of Jiang'an. Hui inherited his original rank as fifth-rank viscount of Shiping.

sentences.zh: 元徽末，為黃門郎，東陽太守。

translations.literal: At the end of Yuanhui he served as Attendant of the Yellow Gate and Administrator of Dongyang.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of Yuanhui he served as attendant of the yellow gate and administrator of Dongyang.

sentences.zh: 繢女適武帝寵子安陸王子敬，永明二年納妃，修外舅姑之敬。

translations.literal: Hui's daughter married the favored son of Emperor Wu, Prince of Anlu Zijing; in the second year of Yongming she entered as consort and cultivated respect toward her wife's parents.
translations.idiomatic: Hui's daughter married the favored son of Emperor Wu, Prince of Anlu Zijing. In the second year of Yongming she entered as consort and cultivated respect toward her wife's parents.

sentences.zh: 武帝遣文惠太子相隨往繢家，置酒設樂，公卿皆冠冕而去，當世榮之。

translations.literal: Emperor Wu sent Crown Prince Wenhuì to follow and go to Hui's house, set out wine and music; dukes and ministers all went in caps and robes; the age honored it.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu sent Crown Prince Wenhuì to follow and go to Hui's house, set out wine and music. Dukes and ministers all went in caps and robes. The age honored it.

sentences.zh: 繢弟約，齊明帝世數年廢錮。

translations.literal: Hui's younger brother Yue was imprisoned and confined several years in Emperor Ming of Qi's age.
translations.idiomatic: Hui's younger brother Yue was imprisoned and confined several years in Emperor Ming of Qi's age.

sentences.zh: 梁武帝時為太子中庶子，嘗謂約曰：「卿方當富貴，必不容久滯屈。

translations.literal: In Emperor Wu of Liang's time he served as Junior Mentor of the Heir Apparent and once said to Yue, "You are about to be rich and noble and surely cannot long remain bent and constrained."
translations.idiomatic: In Emperor Wu of Liang's time he served as junior mentor of the heir apparent and once said to Yue, "You are about to be rich and noble and surely cannot long remain bent and constrained."

sentences.zh: 」及帝作輔，謂曰：「我嘗相卿當富貴，不言卿今日富貴便當見由。

translations.literal: When the emperor became regent he said, "I once judged you would be rich and noble — I did not say that once you were rich and noble you would immediately be seen through because of it."
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor became regent he said, "I once judged you would be rich and noble — I did not say that once you were rich and noble you would immediately be seen through because of it."

sentences.zh: 」曆侍中，左戶尚書，廷尉。

translations.literal: He successively served as Attendant-in-Ordinary, Director of the Left Households, and Court Director of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: He successively served as attendant-in-ordinary, director of the left households, and court director of justice.

sentences.zh: 繢長子雋，不慧，位止建安太守。

translations.literal: Hui's eldest son Jun was not clever and reached only Administrator of Jian'an.
translations.idiomatic: Hui's eldest son Jun was not clever and reached only administrator of Jian'an.

sentences.zh: 雋子克。

translations.literal: Jun's son Ke.
translations.idiomatic: Jun's son was Ke.

sentences.zh: 克美容貌，善容止，仕梁曆司徒右長史、尚書僕射。

translations.literal: Ke had fine appearance and good bearing and deportment; serving Liang he successively reached Right Chief Clerk of the Minister of Education and Vice Director of the Masters of Writing.
translations.idiomatic: Ke had fine appearance and good bearing and deportment. Serving Liang he successively reached right chief clerk of the minister of education and vice director of the masters of writing.

sentences.zh: 台城陷，仕侯景，位太宰、侍中、錄尚書事。

translations.literal: When the terrace city fell he served Hou Jing and reached Grand Mentor, Attendant-in-Ordinary, and Recorder of the Masters of Writing.
translations.idiomatic: When the terrace city fell he served Hou Jing and reached grand mentor, attendant-in-ordinary, and recorder of the masters of writing.

sentences.zh: 景敗，克迎候王僧辯，問克曰：「勞事夷狄之君」，克不能對。

translations.literal: When Jing was defeated Ke went to welcome Wang Sengbian; Sengbian asked Ke, "You toiled serving the barbarian lord" — Ke could not answer.
translations.idiomatic: When Jing was defeated Ke went to welcome Wang Sengbian. Sengbian asked Ke, "You toiled serving the barbarian lord" — Ke could not answer.

sentences.zh: 次問璽紱何在？

translations.literal: Next he asked where the seal cord was.
translations.idiomatic: Next he asked where the seal cord was.

sentences.zh: 克默然良久曰：「趙平原將去。

translations.literal: Ke was silent a long while and said, "Zhao Pingyuan is about to go."
translations.idiomatic: Ke was silent a long while and said, "Zhao Pingyuan is about to go."

sentences.zh: 」平原名思賢，景腹心也，景授平原太守，故克呼焉。

translations.literal: Pingyuan's name was Sixian; he was Jing's trusted heart; Jing appointed him Administrator of Pingyuan — therefore Ke called him thus.
translations.idiomatic: Pingyuan's name was Sixian. He was Jing's trusted heart. Jing appointed him administrator of Pingyuan — therefore Ke called him thus.

sentences.zh: 僧辯乃誚克曰：「王氏百世卿族，便是一朝而墜。

translations.literal: Sengbian then mocked Ke, "The Wang clan for a hundred generations ministerial clan — in one morning it fell."
translations.idiomatic: Sengbian then mocked Ke, "The Wang clan for a hundred generations ministerial clan — in one morning it fell."

sentences.zh: 」仕陳，位尚書右僕射。

translations.literal: Serving Chen he reached Right Vice Director of the Masters of Writing.
translations.idiomatic: Serving Chen he reached right vice director of the masters of writing.

sentences.zh: 桂陽之逼，王道隆為亂兵所殺，蘊力戰，重創禦溝側，或扶以免。

translations.literal: When Guiyang pressed, Wang Daolong was killed by mutinous soldiers; Yun fought hard, was heavily wounded beside the Imperial Moat, and was sometimes supported to escape.
translations.idiomatic: When Guiyang pressed, Wang Daolong was killed by mutinous soldiers. Yun fought hard, was heavily wounded beside the Imperial Moat, and was sometimes supported to escape.

sentences.zh: 事平，撫軍長史褚澄為吳郡太守，司徒左長史蕭惠明言於朝曰：「褚澄開城以納賊，更為股肱大郡，王蘊被甲死戰，棄而不收，賞罰如此，何憂不亂！

translations.literal: When affairs were pacified, Chief Clerk of the Pacifying Army Chu Cheng served as Administrator of Wu commandery; Left Chief Clerk of the Minister of Education Xiao Huiming spoke in court, "Chu Cheng opened the city to admit rebels yet again became trusted arm and thigh of a great commandery; Wang Yun wore armor and died fighting yet was cast aside and not gathered — reward and punishment thus, why worry there will be no chaos!"
translations.idiomatic: When affairs were pacified, Chief Clerk of the Pacifying Army Chu Cheng served as administrator of Wu commandery. Left Chief Clerk of the Minister of Education Xiao Huiming spoke in court, "Chu Cheng opened the city to admit rebels yet again became trusted arm and thigh of a great commandery. Wang Yun wore armor and died fighting yet was cast aside and not gathered — reward and punishment thus, why worry there will be no chaos!"

sentences.zh: 」褚彥回慚，乃議用蘊為湘州刺史。

translations.literal: Chu Yanhui was ashamed and therefore discussed appointing Yun Inspector of Xiang Province.
translations.idiomatic: Chu Yanhui was ashamed and therefore discussed appointing Yun inspector of Xiang Province.

sentences.zh: 及齊高帝輔政，蘊與沈攸之連謀，事敗，斬於秣陵市。

translations.literal: When Emperor Gao of Qi assisted in governance, Yun with Shen Youzhi joined in plot; affairs failed and he was beheaded at Moling market.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Gao of Qi assisted in governance, Yun with Shen Youzhi joined in plot. Affairs failed and he was beheaded at Moling market.

sentences.zh: 奐字道明，彧兄子也。

translations.literal: Huan, styled Daoming, was Yu's elder brother's son.
translations.idiomatic: Huan, styled Daoming, was Yu's elder brother's son.

sentences.zh: 父粹字景深，位黃門侍郎。

translations.literal: His father Cui, styled Jingshen, reached Attendant of the Yellow Gate.
translations.idiomatic: His father Cui, styled Jingshen, reached attendant of the yellow gate.

sentences.zh: 奐繼從祖球，故小字彥孫。

translations.literal: Huan succeeded his younger uncle Qiu and therefore his childhood name was Yansun.
translations.idiomatic: Huan succeeded his younger uncle Qiu and therefore his childhood name was Yansun.

sentences.zh: 年數歲，常侍球許，甚見愛。

translations.literal: Aged several years he constantly attended at Qiu's place and was greatly loved.
translations.idiomatic: Aged several years he constantly attended at Qiu's place and was greatly loved.

sentences.zh: 奐諸兄出身諸王國常侍，而奐起家著作佐郎。

translations.literal: Huan's elder brothers began careers as attendants in princely states, yet Huan began as Assistant in the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Huan's elder brothers began careers as attendants in princely states, yet Huan began as assistant in the secretariat.

sentences.zh: 琅邪顏延之與球情款稍異，常撫奐背曰：「阿奴始免寒士。」

translations.literal: Yan Yanzhi of Langye and Qiu's feeling and generosity were slightly different; he often patted Huan's back and said, "Little fellow, you have at last escaped cold scholar."
translations.idiomatic: Yan Yanzhi of Langye and Qiu's feeling and generosity were slightly different. He often patted Huan's back and said, "Little fellow, you have at last escaped cold scholar."

sentences.zh: 奐少而強濟，叔父景文常以家事委之。

translations.literal: Huan in youth was strong and capable; his uncle Jingwen often entrusted household affairs to him.
translations.idiomatic: Huan in youth was strong and capable. His uncle Jingwen often entrusted household affairs to him.

sentences.zh: 仕宋曆侍中，祠部尚書，轉掌吏部。

translations.literal: Serving Song he successively reached Attendant-in-Ordinary, Director of the Office of Sacrifices, and was transferred to hold the Masters of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: Serving Song he successively reached attendant-in-ordinary, director of the office of sacrifices, and was transferred to hold the masters of personnel.

sentences.zh: 升明初，遷丹陽尹。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Shengming he was transferred to Governor of Danyang.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Shengming he was transferred to governor of Danyang.

sentences.zh: 初，王晏父普曜為沈攸之長史，常懼攸之舉事，不得還，奐為吏部，轉普曜為內職，晏深德之。

translations.literal: At first Wang Yan's father Puyao was Chief Clerk to Shen Youzhi and constantly feared Youzhi would raise affairs and he could not return; Huan was in Personnel and transferred Puyao to inner office; Yan deeply thanked him.
translations.idiomatic: At first Wang Yan's father Puyao was chief clerk to Shen Youzhi and constantly feared Youzhi would raise affairs and he could not return. Huan was in personnel and transferred Puyao to inner office. Yan deeply thanked him.

sentences.zh: 及晏仕齊，武帝以奐宋室外戚，而從弟蘊又同逆，疑有異意，晏叩頭保奐無異志。

translations.literal: When Yan served Qi, Emperor Wu because Huan was maternal kin of the Song outer house and his younger cousin Yun was also together in rebellion suspected different intent; Yan kowtowed guaranteeing Huan had no different will.
translations.idiomatic: When Yan served Qi, Emperor Wu because Huan was maternal kin of the Song outer house and his younger cousin Yun was also together in rebellion suspected different intent. Yan kowtowed guaranteeing Huan had no different will.

sentences.zh: 時晏父母在都，請以為質，武帝乃止。

translations.literal: At the time Yan's parents were in the capital; he requested them as hostages and Emperor Wu then stopped.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Yan's parents were in the capital. He requested them as hostages and Emperor Wu then stopped.

sentences.zh: 永明中，累遷尚書右僕射。

translations.literal: In the Yongming era he was repeatedly promoted to Right Vice Director of the Masters of Writing.
translations.idiomatic: In the Yongming era he was repeatedly promoted to right vice director of the masters of writing.

sentences.zh: 王儉卒，上欲用奐為尚書令，以問晏。

translations.literal: When Wang Jian died the emperor wished to use Huan as Director of the Masters of Writing and asked Yan.
translations.idiomatic: When Wang Jian died the emperor wished to use Huan as director of the masters of writing and asked Yan.

sentences.zh: 晏位遇已重，意不推奐，答曰：「柳世隆有勳望，恐不宜在奐後。

translations.literal: Yan's rank and encounter was already heavy; his mind did not promote Huan and he answered, "Liu Shilong has merit and expectation — I fear he should not be after Huan."
translations.idiomatic: Yan's rank and encounter was already heavy. His mind did not promote Huan and he answered, "Liu Shilong has merit and expectation — I fear he should not be after Huan."

sentences.zh: 」乃轉左僕射，加給事中。

translations.literal: He was therefore transferred to Left Vice Director and given Giver of Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He was therefore transferred to left vice director and given giver of affairs.

sentences.zh: 出為雍州刺史，加都督。

translations.literal: He went out as Inspector of Yong Province with additional command.
translations.idiomatic: He went out as inspector of Yong Province with additional command.

sentences.zh: 與甯蠻長史劉興祖不睦。

translations.literal: He was not on good terms with Chief Clerk of the Pacified Barbarians Liu Xingzu.
